papers.title: Naked-Eye Visual Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification Method for the Rapid Detection of Chikungunya Virus.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) represents a significant global health threat due to its recent resurgence. This protocol highlights the use of capillary-modified visual loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) technology for the rapid detection of CHIKV. We employed Vero cells for virus propagation and utilized the MolPure Viral DNA/RNA Kit for nucleic acid extraction, successfully amplifying extracted viral RNA at 63°C for 25 min. The presence of CHIKV was indicated by a distinct yellowish-green color change, demonstrating the effectiveness and simplicity of this protocol. Our protocol underscores the potential of LAMP technology as a rapid diagnostic tool for CHIKV, enabling timely public health interventions.

analysis.summary_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) poses a growing global health threat, prompting the development of a rapid detection method. Researchers established an in vitro protocol using Vero cells to propagate CHIKV, extracted viral RNA with the MolPure kit, and performed loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) at 63 °C for 25 minutes. Detection relied on a distinct yellowish-green color change, confirming CHIKV presence and demonstrating the assay’s simplicity and effectiveness. The authors interpret this as a promising rapid diagnostic tool that could enable timely public health interventions. By offering a point-of-care, visual LAMP assay, the protocol has the potential to enhance CHIKV surveillance and outbreak response, especially in resource-limited settings. No limitations or evidence strength assessments were reported in the abstract.

papers.title: In Silico Drug Design of Chikungunya Antivirals: Using Consensus Methods for Virtual Screening.
papers.abstract: Structure-based virtual screening is an attractive strategy in drug design. It enables the selection of potential binders to target biomolecules with known molecular structures, providing a rational framework for studying their mechanisms of action and guiding further optimization. However, accurately predicting the free energy of binding remains an extremely challenging task, and the available tools only provide approximate estimates. In this context, one strategy to improve the predictive power of virtual screening and increase the probability of identifying true binders is to employ multiple docking algorithms and combine their results using a consensus method. In this chapter, we will describe a step-by-step methodology to perform this task. We will conduct a virtual screening using AutoDock Vina, AutoDock4, and LeDock, and then combine their results employing the Exponential Consensus Ranking algorithm. Finally, we will discuss possible extensions of this strategy, such as incorporating Molecular Dynamics simulations as an additional filter in the virtual screening or integrating the novel Artificial Intelligence-based methodologies into the consensus framework.

papers.title: Expression and Purification of nsP2 Protease of Chikungunya Virus.
papers.abstract: The nonstructural protein 2 (nsP2) of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an essential cysteine protease involved in viral polyprotein processing and replication complex regulation. Biochemical and structural studies of nsP2 require the availability of highly pure and enzymatically active protein. In this chapter, we describe a straightforward protocol for the heterologous expression and purification of CHIKV nsP2 protease domain (nsP2pro) in Escherichia coli. The protein is expressed at low temperature as a His-tagged construct and purified under native conditions by immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography, followed by dialysis for buffer exchange. The procedure typically yields milligram quantities of highly pure (>95%) and active nsP2pro, and has been successfully applied to wild-type and mutant variants for enzymatic assays and inhibitor screening.

papers.title: Chikungunya Virus Infection in Paraffin-Embedded Tissue: Analysis of Histological Alterations and Viral Detection by Immunohistochemistry.
papers.abstract: Histopathological analysis of tissues infected with Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), including biopsy and autopsy specimens, can provide valuable insights into the pathogenesis of atypical and fatal cases. By examining tissue architecture and cellular alterations under the microscope, it is possible to identify patterns of injury, inflammation, and cellular degeneration. These morphological findings provide evidence of how the pathogen interacts with host cells and tissues. Moreover, immunohistochemistry may be performed in tissue sections for the detection of viral antigens. Importantly, this technique allows the characterization of diverse biologically relevant targets in tissue samples, such as distinct immune cell subsets, cytokines, and additional molecular markers. This is accomplished by the use of antibodies selected for their specificity toward the antigen of interest. In this chapter, we present a concise overview of how histological analysis and immunohistochemical approaches can enhance the understanding of CHIKV-associated pathological mechanisms.

papers.title_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒 石蜡包埋组织中的感染:通过免疫组织化学分析组织学改变和病毒检测。
papers.source_body_en: Histopathological analysis of tissues infected with Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), including biopsy and autopsy specimens, can provide valuable insights into the pathogenesis of atypical and fatal cases. By examining tissue architecture and cellular alterations under the microscope, it is possible to identify patterns of injury, inflammation, and cellular degeneration. These morphological findings provide evidence of how the pathogen interacts with host cells and tissues. Moreover, immunohistochemistry may be performed in tissue sections for the detection of viral antigens. Importantly, this technique allows the characterization of diverse biologically relevant targets in tissue samples, such as distinct immune cell subsets, cytokines, and additional molecular markers. This is accomplished by the use of antibodies selected for their specificity toward the antigen of interest. In this chapter, we present a concise overview of how histological analysis and immunohistochemical approaches can enhance the understanding of CHIKV-associated pathological mechanisms.

papers.title: Assessing Chikungunya Virus Protease Activity and Pharmacological Inhibition Using the acc-CHIK 15 -dnp Fluorogenic Peptide Substrate.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus, a mosquito-borne alphavirus, poses a significant global health threat due to its rapid spread and lack of approved antiviral therapies. The viral nonstructural protein 2 protease (nsP2p) plays a critical role in processing the viral polyprotein to produce key viral enzymes, making it an attractive target for drug development. In this study, we describe the expression and purification of recombinant CHIKV nsP2 protease and establish a robust fluorogenic assay to measure its enzymatic activity using the acc-CHIK 15 -dnp peptide substrate. The assay enables real-time monitoring of proteolytic cleavage and provides a platform for evaluating small-molecule inhibitors. We present optimized conditions for protein expression in E. coli, affinity purification, and tag removal, achieving high-purity nsP2 protease suitable for biochemical characterization. Using this system, we also provide a robust protocol for determining IC50 values for candidate inhibitors. This work provides a reproducible methodology for high-throughput screening of CHIKV protease inhibitors, facilitating the discovery of potential antiviral compounds against chikungunya virus.

papers.title: Quantification of Chikungunya Virus RNA by Real-Time RT-PCR Assay.
papers.abstract: RT-qPCR is characterized by‌ high sensitivity, strong specificity, excellent reproducibility, and operational simplicity, ‌enabling‌ rapid quantification of viral RNA within a short timeframe. The real-time PCR system relies upon the measurement of a fluorescent reporter during PCR, in which the amount of emitted fluorescence is directly proportional to the amount of the PCR product in a reaction. Here, we describe the use of TaqMan® probe-based one-tube Real-time reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) for the detection and quantification of the Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) RNA.

papers.title: Determination of Chikungunya Virus Infectious Titer Using Plaque Assays.
papers.abstract: The plaque-forming assay is the gold-standard method for measuring infectious viral particles. In this technique, lytic viruses infect and destroy host cells, but their spread is restricted by a viscous overlay medium. As a result, new viral particles can only infect neighboring cells, leading to localized clear areas known as plaques, which become visible after staining the remaining living cells. The number of plaques reflects the number of infectious viral particles initially present in the sample and is reported as plaque-forming units (PFU) per sample volume. In this protocol, we describe step by step how to perform a plaque-forming assay to determine the concentration of chikungunya virus in a cell culture supernatant.

papers.title_zh: 使用噬菌斑测定法测定 基孔肯雅病毒 感染滴度。
papers.source_body_en: The plaque-forming assay is the gold-standard method for measuring infectious viral particles. In this technique, lytic viruses infect and destroy host cells, but their spread is restricted by a viscous overlay medium. As a result, new viral particles can only infect neighboring cells, leading to localized clear areas known as plaques, which become visible after staining the remaining living cells. The number of plaques reflects the number of infectious viral particles initially present in the sample and is reported as plaque-forming units (PFU) per sample volume. In this protocol, we describe step by step how to perform a plaque-forming assay to determine the concentration of chikungunya virus in a cell culture supernatant.

papers.title: Automated Counting of Chikungunya Virus-Formed Plaques.
papers.abstract: The cytopathic effect (CPE) is a key to understanding the pathogenicity of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and is useful for evaluating viral infectivity in vitro. The plaque assay, based on the CPE induced by viral infection, provides an infectious virus titer for test samples. Additionally, the assay is simple, quantitative, and cost-effective. Thus, the plaque assay remains the gold standard for determining the infectivity of CHIKV. However, manually counting of virus-induced plaques with the naked eye or under the microscope is often time-consuming and labor-intensive. Therefore, automated plaque-counting software would improve the consistency and efficiency of plaque counting. We recently developed plaQuest, a stand-alone Windows software that enables rapid, reliable plaque counting for CHIKV. In this chapter, we describe the basic procedure for detecting and counting the CHIKV-formed plaques in a 24-well plate.

papers.title: Socio-environmental assessment of Aedes aegypti distribution and risk of chikungunya in vulnerable community.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, poses a major public health challenge in tropical regions. In Brazil, its incidence has increased, especially in socioeconomically vulnerable areas, where environmental conditions favor the proliferation of vectors. Our objective was to assess the socioeconomic and environmental vulnerabilities associated with the spatial distribution of a) Ae. aegypti and b) resident exposure to CHIKV in a low-income community. Identifying key exposure hotspots, our work improves our understanding of CHIKV transmission in informal settlements and facilitates community-based interventions to mitigate CHIKV risk. aegypti using ovitraps and conducted a serological survey from October 2021 to June 2022 in a vulnerable informal community in Salvador, Brazil. Blood samples and sociodemographic, household, and environmental data were collected from residents aged ≥5 years. CHIKV serology was performed, and spatial models using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation assessed vector distribution, seropositivity, and associated factors. Our high-resolution study identified fine-scale vulnerabilities linked to both Ae. aegypti abundance and heightened risk of CHIKV transmission. Based on our findings, effective control strategies should not only focus on traditional methods such as enhancing basic urban infrastructure and services and promoting community awareness, but also target specific breeding sites around homes, address garbage accumulation, and consider the influence of micro-scale temperature variations. These results emphasize the importance of tailored, neighborhood-specific interventions to effectively reduce chikungunya transmission in high-risk communities.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们的目标是评估与Aedes aegypti空间分布以及居民基孔肯雅热暴露相关的社会经济和环境脆弱性,在巴西萨尔瓦多的一个低收入社区中进行。

elements_zh.main_results: 我们的高分辨率研究识别了与埃及伊蚊数量和基孔肯雅热传播风险相关的微尺度脆弱性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 通过识别关键暴露热点,我们的工作提高了我们对基孔肯雅热在非正式聚居区传播机制的理解,并有助于制定基于社区的干预措施以减轻基孔肯雅热风险。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果强调了针对高风险社区制定特定于社区的干预措施的重要性,以有效减少基孔肯雅热的传播。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其仅关注单一社区,可能无法推广到其他环境。此外,使用血清学数据可能无法完全捕捉近期感染情况,且本研究未包括基孔肯雅病毒的分子检测。

papers.abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)通过埃及伊蚊传播,在热带地区构成重大的公共卫生挑战。在巴西,其传播范围不断扩大,尤其是在社会经济脆弱地区,环境条件有利于媒介的繁殖。我们的目标是评估与Aedes aegypti空间分布以及居民基孔肯雅热暴露相关的社会经济和环境脆弱性。通过识别关键暴露热点,我们的工作提高了我们对基孔肯雅热在非正式聚居区传播机制的理解,并有助于制定基于社区的干预措施以减轻基孔肯雅热风险。在巴西萨尔瓦多的一个易感非正式社区中,使用卵笼捕捉埃及伊蚊,并于2021年10月至2022年6月期间对年龄≥5岁的居民进行了血清学调查。收集了居民的血液样本以及社会人口学、家庭和环境数据。进行了基孔肯雅病毒的血清学检测,并使用集成嵌套拉普拉斯近似法(Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation)的空间模型评估了媒介的分布、血清阳性率及相关因素。我们的高分辨率研究识别了与埃及伊蚊数量和基孔肯雅热传播风险相关的微尺度脆弱性。基于我们的研究结果,有效的控制策略不仅应关注传统的增强基本城市基础设施和服务以及促进社区意识的方法,还应针对家庭周围的特定繁殖场所,解决垃圾堆积问题,并考虑微尺度温度变化的影响。这些结果强调了针对高风险社区制定特定于社区的干预措施的重要性,以有效减少基孔肯雅热的传播。

papers.title: Effect of long-term storage on the morphology and infectivity of purified Chikungunya virus
papers.abstract: Abstract Purification and long-term preservation of viral particles are critical steps in virology research, as they directly influence the reliability of structural studies and functional assays supporting vaccine and therapeutic development. Many of these applications, particularly cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and biophysical analyses, require cryoprotectant-free (CPA-free) viral preparations, yet preserving both infectivity and structural integrity under such conditions is especially challenging for enveloped viruses. Here, we describe and validate a practical methodology for purifying and preserving infectious Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) particles for applications in which cryoprotectants cannot be used. CHIKV particles produced in Vero cells were purified by polyethylene glycol (PEG) precipitation followed by discontinuous cesium chloride (CsCl) gradient ultracentrifugation, yielding highly purified preparations with a 70.4% recovery rate and preserved virion morphology, as confirmed by SDS-PAGE, RT-qPCR and negative-staining transmission electron microscopy (TEM). To determine whether freezing rate and ultra-low storage temperature affect long-term preservation, purified CHIKV was subjected to three CPA-free freezing/storage protocols: fast freezing and storage in liquid nitrogen, fast freezing followed by storage at -80°C, and controlled slow freezing followed by storage at -80°C. Infectivity was monitored by plaque assay for up to 202 days post-freezing. Although infectivity declined progressively, no significant differences were observed among the protocols tested, indicating that controlled slow freezing at -80°C is a practical and cost-effective alternative to liquid nitrogen storage. TEM showed preservation of the overall virion morphology under all storage conditions despite the reduced infectivity, suggesting that subtle structural alterations may escape detection by conventional electron microscopy.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of preserving the infectivity and structural integrity of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) particles without the use of cryoprotectants, which are critical for reliable structural studies and functional assays in vaccine and therapeutic development.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved purifying CHIKV particles from Vero cells and subjecting them to three CPA-free freezing/storage protocols to evaluate their long-term preservation under different conditions.
analysis.methods: CHIKV particles were purified using polyethylene glycol (PEG) precipitation and discontinuous cesium chloride (CsCl) gradient ultracentrifugation. Infectivity was assessed using plaque assay, and virion morphology was evaluated by negative-staining transmission electron microscopy (TEM).
analysis.main_results: Purified CHIKV particles showed a 70.4% recovery rate and preserved virion morphology across all storage conditions. However, infectivity declined progressively over time, with no significant differences observed among the tested protocols.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that controlled slow freezing at -80°C is a practical and cost-effective alternative to liquid nitrogen storage for preserving CHIKV infectivity without cryoprotectants, as no significant differences in preservation were found among the protocols.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a reliable method for preserving CHIKV particles for structural and functional studies, which can support vaccine and therapeutic development without the need for cryoprotectants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to abstract-only evidence, and the results were based on a single protocol comparison. The evidence is moderate, as the findings are based on observed infectivity decline and morphology preservation without long-term follow-up or additional validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of freezing rate and ultra-low storage temperature on the preservation of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infectivity and morphology without cryoprotectants. The authors developed a methodology involving polyethylene glycol (PEG) precipitation and discontinuous cesium chloride (CsCl) gradient ultracentrifugation to purify CHIKV particles. They tested three freezing/storage protocols: fast freezing and storage in liquid nitrogen, fast freezing followed by storage at -80°C, and controlled slow freezing followed by storage at -80°C. The results showed that infectivity declined progressively over time, but no significant differences were observed among the protocols. The authors concluded that controlled slow freezing at -80°C is a practical and cost-effective alternative to liquid nitrogen storage for preserving CHIKV. The study's findings have implications for virology research, particularly in vaccine and therapeutic development, by offering a method that avoids the use of cryoprotectants. However, the evidence is based solely on abstract information, which limits its strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决在不使用冷冻保护剂的情况下保持基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)颗粒的感染力和结构完整性的挑战,因为冷冻保护剂对于支持疫苗和治疗开发的可靠结构研究和功能实验至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及从Vero细胞中纯化CHIKV颗粒,并将其置于三种无冷冻保护剂的冷冻/储存方案中,以评估其在不同条件下的长期保存效果。
elements_zh.methods: CHIKV颗粒通过聚乙二醇(PEG)沉淀和不连续铯氯化物(CsCl)梯度超速离心进行纯化。感染力通过斑块实验进行评估,病毒颗粒形态则通过负染色传播电子显微镜(TEM)进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 纯化的CHIKV颗粒在所有储存条件下均表现出70.4%的回收率,并且病毒颗粒形态得以保留。然而,感染力随时间逐渐下降,且在所测试的方案中未观察到显著差异。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,在-80°C下进行控制缓慢冷冻是一种实用且成本效益高的替代液氮储存方法,用于在不使用冷冻保护剂的情况下保存CHIKV感染力,因为在所测试的方案中未发现保存效果的显著差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为在不使用冷冻保护剂的情况下保存CHIKV颗粒提供了可靠的方法,从而支持了结构和功能研究,进而有助于疫苗和治疗开发。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅基于摘要证据,且结果基于单一方案的比较。证据强度中等,因为这些发现基于观察到的感染力下降和形态保存,而没有长期随访或额外验证。

papers.title_zh: 长期储存对纯化基孔肯雅病毒形态和感染力的影响
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Purification and long-term preservation of viral particles are critical steps in virology research, as they directly influence the reliability of structural studies and functional assays supporting vaccine and therapeutic development. Many of these applications, particularly cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and biophysical analyses, require cryoprotectant-free (CPA-free) viral preparations, yet preserving both infectivity and structural integrity under such conditions is especially challenging for enveloped viruses. Here, we describe and validate a practical methodology for purifying and preserving infectious Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) particles for applications in which cryoprotectants cannot be used. CHIKV particles produced in Vero cells were purified by polyethylene glycol (PEG) precipitation followed by discontinuous cesium chloride (CsCl) gradient ultracentrifugation, yielding highly purified preparations with a 70.4% recovery rate and preserved virion morphology, as confirmed by SDS-PAGE, RT-qPCR and negative-staining transmission electron microscopy (TEM). To determine whether freezing rate and ultra-low storage temperature affect long-term preservation, purified CHIKV was subjected to three CPA-free freezing/storage protocols: fast freezing and storage in liquid nitrogen, fast freezing followed by storage at -80°C, and controlled slow freezing followed by storage at -80°C. Infectivity was monitored by plaque assay for up to 202 days post-freezing. Although infectivity declined progressively, no significant differences were observed among the protocols tested, indicating that controlled slow freezing at -80°C is a practical and cost-effective alternative to liquid nitrogen storage. TEM showed preservation of the overall virion morphology under all storage conditions despite the reduced infectivity, suggesting that subtle structural alterations may escape detection by conventional electron microscopy.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 病毒颗粒的纯化和长期保存是病毒学研究中的关键步骤,因为它们直接影响支持疫苗和治疗开发的结构研究和功能实验的可靠性。许多这些应用,特别是冷冻电子显微镜(cryo-EM)和生物物理分析,需要无冷冻保护剂(CPA-free)的病毒制备,但在这种条件下保持感染力和结构完整性对包膜病毒来说尤为具有挑战性。在这里,我们描述并验证了一种实用的方法,用于纯化和保存不使用冷冻保护剂的感染性基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)颗粒。从Vero细胞中生产的CHIKV颗粒通过聚乙二醇(PEG)沉淀和不连续铯氯化物(CsCl)梯度超速离心进行纯化,获得了高纯度的制备,回收率为70.4%,并且病毒颗粒形态得以保留,这通过SDS-PAGE、RT-qPCR和负染色传播电子显微镜(TEM)确认。为了确定冷冻速率和超低温储存条件对长期保存的影响,纯化的CHIKV被置于三种无冷冻保护剂的冷冻/储存方案中:快速冷冻并储存在液氮中、快速冷冻后储存在-80°C、以及控制缓慢冷冻后储存在-80°C。感染力通过冻后202天内的斑块实验进行监测。尽管感染力随时间逐渐下降,但在所测试的方案中未观察到显著差异,这表明在-80°C下进行控制缓慢冷冻是一种实用且成本效益高的替代液氮储存的方法。TEM显示在所有储存条件下病毒颗粒的整体形态均得以保留,尽管感染力有所下降,这表明细微的结构变化可能无法通过常规电子显微镜检测到。
papers.summary_zh: 摘要 病毒颗粒的纯化和长期保存是病毒学研究中的关键步骤,因为它们直接影响支持疫苗和治疗开发的结构研究和功能实验的可靠性。许多这些应用,特别是冷冻电子显微镜(cryo-EM)和生物物理分析,需要无冷冻保护剂(CPA-free)的病毒制备,但在这种条件下保持感染力和结构完整性对包膜病毒来说尤为具有挑战性。在这里,我们描述并验证了一种实用的方法,用于纯化和保存不使用冷冻保护剂的感染性基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)颗粒。从Vero细胞中生产的CHIKV颗粒通过聚乙二醇(PEG)沉淀和不连续铯氯化物(CsCl)梯度超速离心进行纯化,获得了高纯度的制备,回收率为70.4%,并且病毒颗粒形态得以保留,这通过SDS-PAGE、RT-qPCR和负染色传播电子显微镜(TEM)确认。为了确定冷冻速率和超低温储存条件对长期保存的影响,纯化的CHIKV被置于三种无冷冻保护剂的冷冻/储存方案中:快速冷冻并储存在液氮中、快速冷冻后储存在-80°C、以及控制缓慢冷冻后储存在-80°C。感染力通过冻后202天内的斑块实验进行监测。尽管感染力随时间逐渐下降,但在所测试的方案中未观察到显著差异,这表明在-80°C下进行控制缓慢冷冻是一种实用且成本效益高的替代液氮储存的方法。TEM显示在所有储存条件下病毒颗粒的整体形态均得以保留,尽管感染力有所下降,这表明细微的结构变化可能无法通过常规电子显微镜检测到。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决在不使用冷冻保护剂的情况下保持基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)颗粒的感染力和结构完整性的挑战,因为冷冻保护剂对于支持疫苗和治疗开发的可靠结构研究和功能实验至关重要。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及从Vero细胞中纯化CHIKV颗粒,并将其置于三种无冷冻保护剂的冷冻/储存方案中,以评估其在不同条件下的长期保存效果。
analysis_zh.methods: CHIKV颗粒通过聚乙二醇(PEG)沉淀和不连续铯氯化物(CsCl)梯度超速离心进行纯化。感染力通过斑块实验进行评估,病毒颗粒形态则通过负染色传播电子显微镜(TEM)进行分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 纯化的CHIKV颗粒在所有储存条件下均表现出70.4%的回收率,并且病毒颗粒形态得以保留。然而,感染力随时间逐渐下降,且在所测试的方案中未观察到显著差异。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,在-80°C下进行控制缓慢冷冻是一种实用且成本效益高的替代液氮储存方法,用于在不使用冷冻保护剂的情况下保存CHIKV感染力,因为在所测试的方案中未发现保存效果的显著差异。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为在不使用冷冻保护剂的情况下保存CHIKV颗粒提供了可靠的方法,从而支持了结构和功能研究,进而有助于疫苗和治疗开发。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅基于摘要证据,且结果基于单一方案的比较。证据强度中等,因为这些发现基于观察到的感染力下降和形态保存,而没有长期随访或额外验证。

papers.title: Chikungunya Awareness and Related Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Among Nursing Students at the University of Palermo, Italy: A Cross-Sectional Study of Associated Sociodemographic Factors
papers.abstract: Introduction: Chikungunya is an emerging mosquito-borne viral disease that has become a growing public health concern worldwide. Despite documented autochthonous outbreaks in Italy and the increasing spread of Aedes albopictus mosquitoes across Europe, little is known about awareness of chikungunya among future healthcare professionals. This study aimed to assess awareness of chikungunya and evaluate related knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAPs) among nursing students at the University of Palermo, Italy. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted in May 2026 among undergraduate nursing students enrolled at the University of Palermo. Data were collected through an anonymous self-administered online questionnaire investigating sociodemographic characteristics, awareness of chikungunya, sources of information, and KAP related to the disease. Associations between awareness and participant characteristics were assessed using chi-square tests and prevalence ratio analyses. Results: A total of 894 students participated (mean age: 22.33 ± 4.53 years; 72.3% female). Overall, only 22 students (2.46%) reported having previously heard of chikungunya. In a multivariable exploratory analysis, third-year students had a higher prevalence of previous awareness compared with first-year students (PR = 3.38; 95% CI: 1.10–10.36), whereas no statistically significant association was observed for age (PR = 1.07; 95% CI: 1.00–1.15). Mass media represented the main source of information (63.6%), followed by university lectures (22.7%). Among participants who reported previous awareness, responses suggested relatively good recognition of major clinical manifestations, although important gaps were observed regarding vector recognition and transmission pathways. papers.abstract_zh: 引言:基孔肯雅热是一种新兴的蚊媒病毒性疾病,已成为全球日益严重的公共卫生问题。尽管在意大利已记录到本地传播的基孔肯雅病毒,且欧洲范围内白纹伊蚊的传播范围不断扩大,但关于未来医疗专业人员对基孔肯雅热的认知仍知之甚少。本研究旨在评估护理专业学生对基孔肯雅热的认知,并评估其相关知识、态度和行为(KAPs)。方法:2026年5月,在意大利帕勒莫大学进行了一项横断面研究,调查在读护理专业本科生。通过匿名的自我管理在线问卷收集数据,内容涉及社会人口学特征、基孔肯雅热的认知、信息来源以及与该疾病相关的KAP。使用卡方检验和比值比分析评估认知与参与者特征之间的关联。结果:共有894名学生参与(平均年龄:22.33 ± 4.53岁;72.3%为女性)。总体而言,仅有22名学生(2.46%)表示之前听说过基孔肯雅热。在多变量探索性分析中,第三年学生比第一年学生有更高的基孔肯雅热认知比值比(PR = 3.38;95% CI:1.10–10.36),而年龄与认知之间未观察到统计学显著关联(PR = 1.07;95% CI:1.00–1.15)。大众媒体是主要的信息来源(63.6%),其次是大学课程(22.7%)。在报告过基孔肯雅热认知的参与者中,其对主要临床表现的识别相对较好,但关于基孔肯雅病毒传播途径的识别仍存在重要差距。参与者对预防的态度总体积极,大多数参与者报告采用了推荐的蚊虫控制措施。结论:护理专业学生对基孔肯雅热的认知极低。在护理课程中加强关于新兴蚊媒病毒的教育干预,可能有助于提高应对能力、风险沟通能力和未来的公共卫生响应水平。

papers.title: Alphavirus Nsp3 protein hijacks receptor-mediated mitophagy via BNIP3L/NIX to dampen IFN response and promote viral replication
papers.abstract: Alphaviruses encompass a variety of human and animal pathogens, such as getah virus (GETV), chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and Sindbis virus (SINV). Increasing evidence suggests that innate immunity plays an important role in host resistance to alphavirus infection, while alphaviruses have evolved multiple strategies to evade host antiviral innate immunity. Mitochondria, as key immune hubs, play a central role in the initiation of innate antiviral responses. It remains unclear whether alphaviruses inhibit innate immune responses by manipulating mitochondria. In this study, we found that GETV infection damages mitochondrial structure and function, as shown by mitochondrial membrane potential depolarization, reduction in mitochondrial numbers, and an imbalance in mitochondrial dynamics. GETV infection induces mitophagy in host cells and promotes viral replication. Nsp3 protein of alphaviruses (CHIKV, SINV, GETV) can directly trigger receptor-mediated mitophagy through its interaction with BNIP3L/NIX. Knockdown of BNIP3L could alleviate mitophagy caused by GETV infection. Mitophagy induced by alphavirus Nsp3 protein leads to degradation of MAVS which inhibits the IFN response and promotes viral replication. Collectively, our results demonstrated that alphaviruses Nsp3 serves as a novel virulence factor, inducing BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy to degrade MAVS and evade the host immune response.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate whether alphaviruses inhibit innate immune responses by manipulating mitochondria, as it remains unclear how these viruses interact with host immune mechanisms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on alphaviruses, specifically Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and examined their effects on host cell mitochondria and immune responses in vitro and in vivo.
analysis.methods: The researchers used molecular and cellular techniques to assess mitochondrial structure and function, including measuring mitochondrial membrane potential, mitochondrial numbers, and dynamics. They also evaluated mitophagy and its impact on MAVS degradation and IFN response.
analysis.main_results: The study found that CHIKV infection damages mitochondrial structure and function, as evidenced by mitochondrial membrane potential depolarization, reduction in mitochondrial numbers, and an imbalance in mitochondrial dynamics. Additionally, CHIKV infection induces mitophagy, which promotes viral replication.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that the Nsp3 protein of alphaviruses, including CHIKV, induces BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy to degrade MAVS, thereby inhibiting the IFN response and promoting viral replication. This represents a novel mechanism by which alphaviruses evade host immunity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide insights into the molecular mechanisms by which CHIKV evades host immunity, which could inform future research on antiviral strategies and improve understanding of CHIKV pathogenesis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro and in vivo models, and the evidence is based on abstract-only data. However, the results are supported by direct observations and molecular analyses, suggesting a moderate level of confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) interacts with host mitochondria and immune responses. It explores whether CHIKV manipulates mitochondria to inhibit innate immunity, a critical aspect of viral pathogenesis. The research reveals that CHIKV infection damages mitochondrial structure and function, leading to mitophagy and degradation of MAVS, which suppresses the IFN response and enhances viral replication. These findings highlight a novel mechanism by which CHIKV evades host immunity, offering potential insights for future antiviral strategies. The study is based on in vitro and in vivo models, and while the evidence is moderate, it contributes to understanding the molecular basis of CHIKV infection and its impact on host immune responses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查甲病毒是否通过操纵线粒体来抑制先天性 免疫应答,因为目前尚不清楚这些病毒如何与 宿主 免疫机制相互作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究重点关注甲病毒,特别是 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV),并在体外和体内检查了它们对 宿主 细胞线粒体和 免疫应答 的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用分子和细胞技术来评估线粒体结构和功能,包括测量线粒体膜电位、线粒体数量和动力学。他们还评估了线粒体自噬及其对 MAVS 降解和 IFN 反应的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究发现,CHIKV 感染会损害线粒体的结构和功能,表现为线粒体膜电位去极化、线粒体数量减少和线粒体动力学失衡。此外,CHIKV 感染会诱导线粒体自噬,从而促进病毒复制。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为甲病毒(包括 CHIKV)的 Nsp3 蛋白诱导 BNIP3L 介导的线粒体自噬以降解 MAVS 的证据,从而抑制 IFN 反应并促进病毒复制。这代表了甲病毒逃避 宿主 免疫的新机制。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提供了对 CHIKV 逃避 宿主 免疫的分子机制的见解,这可以为未来 抗病毒药物 策略的研究提供信息,并提高对 CHIKV 发病机制 的理解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外和体内模型,证据仅基于抽象数据。然而,这些结果得到了直接观察和分子分析的支持,表明具有中等的置信度。

papers.title: COINFECTION WITH PLASMODIUM VIVAX AND CHIKUNGUNYA; WHEN FEBRILE ILLNESS EVOLVES INTO HYPERDYNAMIC SHOCK: CASE REPORT
papers.abstract: Coinfection with malaria and chikungunya is a rare presentation and poses a diagnostic challenge., especially since both infections can produce systemic manifestations and hemodynamic compromise. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient from an urban area with no known past medical history, who presented with a seven-day history of fever, dizziness, generalized weakness, arthralgia, and vomiting. On admission, she was febrile, tachycardic, and hypotensive, with an insufficient hemodynamic response to initial resuscitation with crystalloids, requiring vasopressor support. Advanced cardiovascular evaluation revealed a predominantly vasodilatory and hyperdynamic profile, characterized by high cardiac output, decreased systemic vascular resistance, and preserved stroke volume. Left and right ventricular systolic and diastolic function remained preserved, with adequate TAPSE and MAPSE, and no significant chamber dilation or regional contractility abnormalities. The electrocardiogram and cardiac enzymes showed no evidence of myocardial injury or myocarditis. Studies revealed severe anemia, with a hemoglobin level of 6 g/ dL, and hepatosplenomegaly. Thick blood smear identified Plasmodium. The patient tested positive for vivax, while the PCR test for chikungunya was positive and the dengue test was negative, confirming the coinfection. Intravenous artesunate was initiated, followed by artemether-lumefantrine, in addition to vasoactive support and transfusion of two units of packed red blood cells. The patient experienced progressive hemodynamic recovery and a favorable clinical course. This case highlights the importance of considering vector-borne coinfections and characterizing the hemodynamic phenotype to differentiate vasodilatory shock from cardiogenic compromise.
papers.journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

papers.abstract_zh: 疟疾和基孔肯雅热的混合感染是一种罕见的表现,对诊断提出了挑战,特别是因为两种感染都会产生全身表现和血流动力学损害。我们介绍了一名来自城市地区的 23 岁女性患者,无既往病史,有 7 天发热、头晕、全身无力、关节痛 和呕吐病史。入院时,她出现发热、心动过速和低血压,对晶体液初始复苏的血流动力学反应不足,需要血管加压药支持。高级心血管评估显示主要是血管舒张和高动力特征,其特征是高心输出量、降低的全身血管阻力和保留的每搏输出量。左心室和右心室收缩和舒张功能仍然保留,具有足够的 TAPSE 和 MAPSE,并且没有明显的心室扩张或局部收缩力异常。心电图和心肌酶显示没有心肌损伤或心肌炎的证据。研究显示严重贫血,血红蛋白水平为 6 g/dL,并且肝脾肿大。厚厚的血涂片鉴定出疟原虫。该患者的间日疟检测呈阳性,而基孔肯雅热PCR检测呈阳性,登革热检测呈阴性,证实了双重感染。开始静脉注射青蒿琥酯,随后使用蒿甲醚-本芴醇,此外还进行血管活性支持和输注两个单位的浓缩红细胞。患者的血流动力学逐渐恢复,临床病程良好。该病例强调了考虑 媒介 传播的合并感染和表征血流动力学表型以区分血管舒张性休克和心源性损害的重要性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在强调间日疟原虫和 基孔肯雅病毒 合并感染带来的诊断挑战,因为两者都会产生全身表现和血流动力学损害。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 病例报告 对一名来自城市地区的 23 岁女性患者进行,该患者无既往病史,表现为发烧、头晕、全身无力、病例报告 和呕吐。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过厚血涂片和PCR检测确认了患者的诊断,分别鉴定出间日疟原虫和基孔肯雅病毒,同时排除了登革热病毒。
analysis_zh.main_results: 高级心血管评估显示出高动力特征,心输出量高,全身血管阻力降低,每搏输出量保持不变。心电图和心肌酶显示没有心肌损伤或心肌炎的证据。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,间日疟原虫和 基孔肯雅病毒 的共感染可导致独特的血流动力学表型,因此需要与其他休克原因仔细区分。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该病例强调了在临床环境中识别 媒介 传播的合并感染的重要性,并强调需要准确的血流动力学特征来指导适当的治疗。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单个病例报告,可能无法推广。然而,鉴于详细的临床和诊断结果,证据是强有力的。

papers.full_text: AbstractChikungunya virus remains a crucial global health issue with no approved therapy available. In particular, the viral replication is associated with the non-structural protein 2 protease (nsP2pro). In this study, possible inhibitors for nsP2pro from the National Cancer Institute (NCI) database were screened via computational approaches. Molecular docking simulations were initially predicted top potential ligands. MD simulations were then performed to refine the ligand binding pose. During the equilibrium intervals, the ligands formed rigid contacts with the residues Asn476, Ala511, Tyr512, Tyr544 and Trp549 of nsP2pro. Moreover, five compounds probably prevent the biological activity of nsP2pro by increasing the distance of Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 pairs. Furthermore, perturbation simulations finally confirmed that NSC 319990, NSC 80731, NSC 80735, NSC 67436 and NSC 37553 compounds exhibited significantly stronger binding affinity, ranging from –9.70 ± 0.61 to –11.71 ± 1.25 kcal mol–1, than that of the available inhibitor RA-0002034, ΔGFEP = − 6.45 ± 0.32 kcal mol–1. Besides, the strong correlation between ΔGFEP and Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 pair suggests that a stronger binding ligand better inhibits the biological activity of nsP2pro. Overall, these findings suggest that five NCI compounds are highly promising candidates for further experimental validation as novel nsP2pro inhibitors.Keywords: chikungunya virus, non-structural protein 2 protease, docking, free energy perturbation, molecular dynamics simulation 2.Material and methods2.1.Chikungunya virus non-structural protein 2 protease and ligand conformationsThe three-dimensional structure of CHIKV nsP2pro was downloaded from the Protein Data Bank (PDB) with PDB ID: 4ZTB) [8]. In total, 1581 trial ligands were obtained from the NCI Diversity Set VII database [33]. Moreover, the three-dimensional structure of RA-0002034 [15], an available inhibitor, of nsP2pro was downloaded from the PubChem database [34] with the corresponding ID of 139018657.2.2.Molecular docking simulationAutoDock Vina [35] with altered empirical parameters [36] was employed to preliminarily investigate the ligand binding pose and affinity to CHIKV nsP2pro. Because 4ZTB contains no native inhibitor, the Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV), an Alphavirus, nsP2pro with the PDB ID 8T8N [37] was employed to accurately characterize the CHIKV nsP2pro active site (cf. figure 1). Chain A of CHIKV nsP2pro, with sequence from 471 to 791, was selected as the docking receptor. The docking grid centre was chosen as centre of mass of the native ligand of VEEV nsP2pro after VEEV nsP2pro + its inhibitors were aligned to CHIKV nsP2pro via PyMOL tools [38]. The docking grid was selected as 20 × 20 × 20 Å, which is big enough to cover the whole of the binding site. The docking simulations were performed with an exhaustiveness value of 8, a setting statistically demonstrated to be sufficient for accurate pose prediction of standard organic ligands in comprehensive benchmarks [36,39]. Here, only one conformation with the strongest binding affinity was recorded. Figure 1.Conformation of CHIKV nsP2pro (green colour) in superposition state with VEEV nsP2pro (grey colour). In particular, the inhibitor of VEEV nsP2pro is denoted with red colour highlight.2.3.Molecular dynamics simulationGROMACS version 2023 [40] was employed to mimic two systems, including the CHIKV nsP2pro + inhibitor and the free inhibitor in solution. Particularly, nsP2pro and neutralized ions were topologized using the Amber99SB-iLDN force field [41]. Consequently, the TIP3P water model was employed to represent the water molecule [42]. The force field was used because it is the most suitable for free energy calculations [43,44]. Both systems—the nsP2pro + inhibitor and the free inhibitor—were inserted into a cubic periodic boundary condition box with a spacing of larger than 1.0 nm between system and boundary. The water molecules and neutralized ions were then inserted into the box. The number of atoms of the complex nsP2pro + inhibitor and the free inhibitor are ca 76 000 and 3660 atoms.Both systems were initially minimized using the steepest descent method. Consequently, the nsP2pro + inhibitor and free inhibitor in solution were positionally constrained in canonical and isobaric-isothermal ensemble simulations of 100 ps each. The outcome conformation was used as the original structure for 200 and 20 ns of MD simulations at 310 K, corresponding to the complexed CHIKV nsP2pro + ligand and the free ligand in solution, respectively. During MD simulations, the coordinates of the solvated systems were recorded every 100 ps. The simulation was repeated three times for each system to guarantee the sampling statistics. In particular, the MD parameters were obtained from the previous studies [45,46]. The non-bonded contact between distinct atoms was updated within 0.9 nm every 30 fs. The electrostatic (cou) and van der Waals (vdW) interactions were calculated using particle-mesh Ewald and cut-off schemes within a range of 0.9 nm, respectively. Moreover, an accurate and efficient leap-frog stochastic dynamics integrator was employed to mimic the behaviour of the solvated systems. The V-rescale thermostat and Parrinello–Rahman extended-ensemble pressure coupling were used during MD simulations.2.4.Perturbation simulationThe free energy perturbation (FEP) simulations can be used to determine the binding free energy between biomolecules with high accuracy [23,47,48]. In particular, during the simulations, the coupling parameter, λ, is used for modifying the systemic Hamiltonian. Thus, a molecule is removed from the solvated system. The difference in free energy change between the two states available, λ = 0, and removed, λ = 1, can be calculated via the Bennett's acceptance ratio approach [49]. The ligand binding free energy can be computed over perturbation simulations as the difference of free energy change in two processes including removing the inhibitor from CHIKV nsP2pro + inhibitor and the free inhibitor in solution. This approach is called the double-annihilation binding free energy method [50,51]. Moreover, in this work, the last snapshot of MD simulations was used as the initial conformation of perturbation simulations. The electrostatic coupling parameter, λcou, was selected as 0.00, 0.10, 0.20, 0.35, 0.50, 0.65, 0.80 and 1.00. Furthermore, the vdW coupling parameter, λvdW, was chosen as 0.00, 0.10, 0.25, 0.35, 0.50, 0.65, 0.75, 0.90 and 1.00. The value of the coupling parameters was chosen in line with the previous studies [23]. In addition, more details about the double-annihilation binding free energy calculations have been previously reported [23,52].2.5.Analysis toolsChemicalize, a tool of ChemAxon, was employed to estimate the inhibitor pKa [53]. A three-dimensional interaction diagram between CHIKV nsP2pro and its ligand was prepared using PLIP web application [54]. Intermolecular sidechain contact is calculated when the non-hydrogen spacing between distinct atoms is smaller than 0.45 nm. Intermolecular hydrogen bond (HB) contact is figured when two conditions are satisfied. The first condition is that the angle, ∠, between donor (D), hydrogen (H) and acceptor (A) must be larger than 135 degrees. The second condition is that the distance between D and A must be smaller than 0.35 nm. The non-hydrogen atoms root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) of the solvated system was calculated via GROMACS tools ‘gmx rms’. The distance between two atoms was computed via GROMACS tools ‘gmx mindist’. The clustering calculation was completed using ‘gmx cluster’ tools with a non-hydrogen atom cut-off of 0.3 nm. The absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion (ADME) and chemical properties of compounds were estimated via pkCSM [55]. Supplementary Material Supplementary Materials 3.Results and discussion3.1.Docking affinity and poseAs mentioned above, the CHIKV nsP2pro is one of the most favoured targets for drug design because it is associated with the viral replication [6]. In particular, the enzyme cleaves the polyproteins and unwinds the RNA. In particular, nsP2pro is a cysteine protease and it can recognize small peptide substrates. Notably, several investigations have characterized small compounds proficient of inhibiting CHIKV nsP2pro, such as RA-0002034 [15]. Besides, the structural compounds can be altered to improve their inhibitory and pharmacokinetic properties [56–58]. Therefore, screening the inhibitor for CHIKV nsP2pro from small compounds is a highly potential area of research. In this context, AutoDock Vina [35], an open-source molecular docking application, is one of the most popular protocols, with more than 28 000 citations to date. A modified version with altered empirical parameters, denoted as mVina, has a higher correlation coefficient, R = 0.62 ± 0.02, compared with the original version, R = 0.54 ± 0.02 [35,36]. The package was thus used to estimate the binding pose and affinity of 1581 NCI compounds to CHIKV nsP2pro. The distribution of the obtained molecular docking energy of these compounds to nsP2pro is shown in figure 2A. Specifically, the docking scores ranged from –4.9 to –13.3 kcal mol–1, with an average of −8.89 ± 1.42 kcal mol–1. The computed error was the standard deviation. Figure 2.(A) Distribution of molecular docking results of 1581 NCI compounds to CHIKV nsP2pro. (B) The superposition of top-lead five NCI ligands and RA-0002034 in docking state with CHIKV nsP2pro. (C) Enlarged perspective of NSC 80731 binding to CHIKV nsP2pro active site, which is obtained via molecular docking simulations. In particular, the catalytic residues were denoted as Cys478, Ser482 and His548. Red dashed lines denote Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 pairs. (D) Interaction diagram between CHIKV nsP2pro and NSC 80731 in docking mode, which was prepared using PLIP web application [54]. (E) MD-refined binding pose of NSC 80731 to CHIKV nsP2pro and the pairs (red dashed lines) including Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548. In particular, the MD-refined structure was obtained through clustering methods. (F) Interaction diagram between CHIKV nsP2pro and NSC 80731 in MD-refined binding mode, which was prepared using PLIP web application [54].Five top-lead compounds with the strongest binding affinity to CHIKV nsP2pro are listed in table 1. Besides, RA-0002034 [15], an available inhibitor of nsP2pro, was also docked to the protease for comparison. The obtained result is also mentioned in table 1, in which the docking energy of –9.9 kcal mol–1 is in good agreement with the experimental value, ΔGEXP = −9.27 kcal mol–1. The outcomes imply that mVina is an appropriate protocol for estimating the possible binding compounds to CHIKV nsP2pro. The binding pose between ligands and nsP2pro is shown in figure 2 and figures S1–S6 in the supplementary material. The docking interaction diagrams suggested that three residues—Tyr544, Asn547 and Leu670—may act as important elements during the ligand binding process because they form HB, hydrophobic or π-stacking contacts to CHIKV nsP2pro. The ligands may indirectly alter the pairs including Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548, as they interact rigidly with the residue Asn547. It should be noted that these pairs are associated with the catalytic domain of the enzyme. Molecular docking outcome implies that five top-lead compounds may act as potential inhibitors for CHIKV nsP2pro. Table 1.The ligand binding affinity provided by molecular docking simulations.ano.ligandΔGDockΔGEXPb1NSC 319990–13.32NSC 80731–13.33NSC 80735–13.34NSC 67436–13.15NSC 37553–13.06RA-0002034 –9.9–9.27 [15]aThe unit of energy is kcal mol–1.bThe experimental binding free energy was calculated via formula ΔGEXP = RTln(Ki), where R is the gas constant, T is the absolute temperature, and Ki is the inhibition constant.3.2.Refining docking results with molecular dynamics simulationsIt should be noted that molecular docking simulations commonly use several approximations and constraints to speed up the calculation process [59–61]. The applied simplifications involved using a rigid receptor, using an implicit solvent model, incorporating a united atom model limiting a number of trail binding pose, etc. [35,60,62,63]. Therefore, although the molecular docking simulations provided an appropriate outcome, MD simulations were then carried out to refine the results. The complexes, including CHIKV nsP2pro + NCI compounds, were parametrized and mimicked using MD simulations. Besides, the CHIKV nsP2pro + RA-0002034 was also investigated because RA-0002034 acts as a positive control. The ligand binding pose and nsP2pro structure changed during MD simulations (cf. figures S1–S6 in the supplementary material). In particular, ligands have established highly optimized and stable networks of HBs and hydrophobic interactions with important active-site residues such as Tyr544, Trp549, Asn547 and Ala511. Thus the binding mechanisms were explored based on structural analyses. Each complex was simulated three times in MD simulations with a length of 200 ns. Furthermore, the free ligand in solution was mimicked for over 20 ns of MD simulations. The binding affinity of ligands to CHIKV nsP2pro was clarified using binding free energy protocols [64,65]. Here, perturbation simulations were acquired to complete this task since providing the most accurate results until the date [66,67]. Notably, this method has a proven track record of successful application across numerous biological targets [45,46,68,69,70].The CHIKV nsP2pro + ligand complexes in solution mostly reached equilibrium conditions after ca 100 ns of MD simulations according to the obtained RMSD presented in table S1 in the supplementary material. Moreover, the free ligand in solution also reached stable states after ca 2.5 ns of MD simulations (cf. supplementary material, table S2). The systemic coordinates within the equilibrium intervals were collected for structural analysis. To clarify the binding picture between nsP2pro and inhibitor, the representative conformations of the complexes in solution were estimated using the clustering method over all equilibrium snapshots. A non-hydrogen atom cut-off of 0.3 nm was applied. The ligand interaction diagrams were then investigated using PLIP web application [54]. The outcomes are described in figure 2 and figures S1–S5 in the supplementary material. MD-refined findings suggested that the residues Asn476, Ala511, Tyr512, Tyr544 and Trp549 act as crucial residues controlling the binding process of nsP2pro inhibitors. Although top-leads and the available inhibitor do not form rigid interactions to Cys478 or Ser482 or His548, the six compounds can change the pairs involving Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 via interacting with Asn476 and Trp549. Indeed, the pairs including Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 were significantly changed when the ligands were induced. The outcomes are described in figure 3 and table S3 in the supplementary material. In particular, the average of the spacing between Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 is 7.4 ± 1.4 and 8.9 ± 1.8 Å, respectively, when the free nsP2pro in solution is considered. When the considered inhibitors were induced, the distances of the pair Cys478-Sγ – Nε-His548 are significantly enlarged compared to the ones of the free nsP2pro in solution and nsP2pro + RA-0002034 systems (cf. supplementary material, table S3). Meanwhile, the distance of the pair Ser482-Oγ - Nε-His548 varies depending on the specific ligand (cf. Table S3 of the Supporting Information). The findings suggest that five NCI compounds can prevent the biological activity of nsP2pro. Figure 3.Distribution of the pairs between Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 (upper panel) and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 (lower panel). The results are obtained by analysing the MD-refined equilibrium snapshots.3.3.Perturbation simulationsThe binding free energy of ligands to CHIKV nsP2pro can be accurately estimated via FEP simulations. During simulations, the coupling parameter λ was changed to turn the system from bound to unbound states. The free energy alteration of the nsP2pro + inhibitor and free inhibitor in solution was computed using λ-alteration simulation. In particular, alchemical free energy profiles of coulomb, vdW and total terms over MD simulations are shown in figure S7 in the supplementary material. Moreover, the smooth ΔG versus λ transitions along with small computed error bars reveal excellent phase-space overlap, proving that the number of applied λ windows is sufficient (cf. supplementary material, figure S8). Furthermore, the free energy difference between two processes is calculated as the binding free energy. The obtained results are described in table 2. The binding free energy of RA-0002034 to nsP2pro via FEP calculations is ΔGFEP = −6.45 ± 0.32 kcal mol–1, which is significantly smaller than the experimental value, ΔGEXP = −9.27 kcal mol–1. The difference may be owing to the fact that only non-covalent binding free energy is taken into account in the calculations. Moreover, all five NCI compounds exhibited significantly larger binding affinities to CHIKV nsP2pro than the available inhibitor named RA-0002034. In particular, the NSC 80731 and NSC 37553 bind to nsP2pro with the strongest binding free energy of –11.71 ± 1.25 and –11.14 ± 0.32 kcal mol–1, respectively. The others including NSC 80735, NSC 67436 and NSC 319990 also unveiled a stronger binding affinity than RA-0002034 with corresponding values of –10.91 ± 2.00, –10.13 ± 0.73 and –9.70 ± 0.61 kcal mol–1, respectively. Five NCI compounds act as highly potential inhibitors as compared with the CHIKV nsP2pro. full_text_sections.methods: 2.Material and methods2.1.Chikungunya virus non-structural protein 2 protease and ligand conformationsThe three-dimensional structure of CHIKV nsP2pro was downloaded from the Protein Data Bank (PDB) with PDB ID: 4ZTB) [8]. In total, 1581 trial ligands were obtained from the NCI Diversity Set VII database [33]. Moreover, the three-dimensional structure of RA-0002034 [15], an available inhibitor, of nsP2pro was downloaded from the PubChem database [34] with the corresponding ID of 139018657.2.2.Molecular docking simulationAutoDock Vina [35] with altered empirical parameters [36] was employed to preliminarily investigate the ligand binding pose and affinity to CHIKV nsP2pro. Because 4ZTB contains no native inhibitor, the Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV), an Alphavirus, nsP2pro with the PDB ID 8T8N [37] was employed to accurately characterize the CHIKV nsP2pro active site (cf. figure 1). Chain A of CHIKV nsP2pro, with sequence from 471 to 791, was selected as the docking receptor. The docking grid centre was chosen as centre of mass of the native ligand of VEEV nsP2pro after VEEV nsP2pro + its inhibitors were aligned to CHIKV nsP2pro via PyMOL tools [38]. The docking grid was selected as 20 × 20 × 20 Å, which is big enough to cover the whole of the binding site. The docking simulations were performed with an exhaustiveness value of 8, a setting statistically demonstrated to be sufficient for accurate pose prediction of standard organic ligands in comprehensive benchmarks [36,39]. Here, only one conformation with the strongest binding affinity was recorded. Figure 1.Conformation of CHIKV nsP2pro (green colour) in superposition state with VEEV nsP2pro (grey colour). In particular, the inhibitor of VEEV nsP2pro is denoted with red colour highlight.2.3.Molecular dynamics simulationGROMACS version 2023 [40] was employed to mimic two systems, including the CHIKV nsP2pro + inhibitor and the free inhibitor in solution. Particularly, nsP2pro and neutralized ions were topologized using the Amber99SB-iLDN force field [41]. Consequently, the TIP3P water model was employed to represent the water molecule [42]. The force field was used because it is the most suitable for free energy calculations [43,44]. Both systems—the nsP2pro + inhibitor and the free inhibitor—were inserted into a cubic periodic boundary condition box with a spacing of larger than 1.0 nm between system and boundary. The water molecules and neutralized ions were then inserted into the box. The number of atoms of the complex nsP2pro + inhibitor and the free inhibitor are ca 76 000 and 3660 atoms.Both systems were initially minimized using the steepest descent method. Consequently, the nsP2pro + inhibitor and free inhibitor in solution were positionally constrained in canonical and isobaric-isothermal ensemble simulations of 100 ps each. The outcome conformation was used as the original structure for 200 and 20 ns of MD simulations at 310 K, corresponding to the complexed CHIKV nsP2pro + ligand and the free ligand in solution, respectively. During MD simulations, the coordinates of the solvated systems were recorded every 100 ps. The simulation was repeated three times for each system to guarantee the sampling statistics. In particular, the MD parameters were obtained from the previous studies [45,46]. The non-bonded contact between distinct atoms was updated within 0.9 nm every 30 fs. The electrostatic (cou) and van der Waals (vdW) interactions were calculated using particle-mesh Ewald and cut-off schemes within a range of 0.9 nm, respectively. Moreover, an accurate and efficient leap-frog stochastic dynamics integrator was employed to mimic the behaviour of the solvated systems. The V-rescale thermostat and Parrinello–Rahman extended-ensemble pressure coupling were used during MD simulations.2.4.Perturbation simulationThe free energy perturbation (FEP) simulations can be used to determine the binding free energy between biomolecules with high accuracy [23,47,48]. In particular, during the simulations, the coupling parameter, λ, is used for modifying the systemic Hamiltonian. Thus, a molecule is removed from the solvated system. The difference in free energy change between the two states available, λ = 0, and removed, λ = 1, can be calculated via the Bennett's acceptance ratio approach [49]. The ligand binding free energy can be computed over perturbation simulations as the difference of free energy change in two processes including removing the inhibitor from CHIKV nsP2pro + inhibitor and the free inhibitor in solution. This approach is called the double-annihilation binding free energy method [50,51]. Moreover, in this work, the last snapshot of MD simulations was used as the initial conformation of perturbation simulations. The electrostatic coupling parameter, λcou, was selected as 0.00, 0.10, 0.20, 0.35, 0.50, 0.65, 0.80 and 1.00. Furthermore, the vdW coupling parameter, λvdW, was chosen as 0.00, 0.10, 0.25, 0.35, 0.50, 0.65, 0.75, 0.90 and 1.00. The value of the coupling parameters was chosen in line with the previous studies [23]. In addition, more details about the double-annihilation binding free energy calculations have been previously reported [23,52].2.5.Analysis toolsChemicalize, a tool of ChemAxon, was employed to estimate the inhibitor pKa [53]. A three-dimensional interaction diagram between CHIKV nsP2pro and its ligand was prepared using PLIP web application [54]. Intermolecular sidechain contact is calculated when the non-hydrogen spacing between distinct atoms is smaller than 0.45 nm. Intermolecular hydrogen bond (HB) contact is figured when two conditions are satisfied. The first condition is that the angle, ∠, between donor (D), hydrogen (H) and acceptor (A) must be larger than 135 degrees. The second condition is that the distance between D and A must be smaller than 0.35 nm. The non-hydrogen atoms root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) of the solvated system was calculated via GROMACS tools ‘gmx rms’. The distance between two atoms was computed via GROMACS tools ‘gmx mindist’. The clustering calculation was completed using ‘gmx cluster’ tools with a non-hydrogen atom cut-off of 0.3 nm. The absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion (ADME) and chemical properties of compounds were estimated via pkCSM [55]. Supplementary Material Supplementary Materials
full_text_sections.results: 3.Results and discussion3.1.Docking affinity and poseAs mentioned above, the CHIKV nsP2pro is one of the most favoured targets for drug design because it is associated with the viral replication [6]. In particular, the enzyme cleaves the polyproteins and unwinds the RNA. In particular, nsP2pro is a cysteine protease and it can recognize small peptide substrates. Notably, several investigations have characterized small compounds proficient of inhibiting CHIKV nsP2pro, such as RA-0002034 [15]. Besides, the structural compounds can be altered to improve their inhibitory and pharmacokinetic properties [56–58]. Therefore, screening the inhibitor for CHIKV nsP2pro from small compounds is a highly potential area of research. In this context, AutoDock Vina [35], an open-source molecular docking application, is one of the most popular protocols, with more than 28 000 citations to date. A modified version with altered empirical parameters, denoted as mVina, has a higher correlation coefficient, R = 0.62 ± 0.02, compared with the original version, R = 0.54 ± 0.02 [35,36]. The package was thus used to estimate the binding pose and affinity of 1581 NCI compounds to CHIKV nsP2pro. The distribution of the obtained molecular docking energy of these compounds to nsP2pro is shown in figure 2A. Specifically, the docking scores ranged from –4.9 to –13.3 kcal mol–1, with an average of −8.89 ± 1.42 kcal mol–1. The computed error was the standard deviation. Figure 2.(A) Distribution of molecular docking results of 1581 NCI compounds to CHIKV nsP2pro. (B) The superposition of top-lead five NCI ligands and RA-0002034 in docking state with CHIKV nsP2pro. (C) Enlarged perspective of NSC 80731 binding to CHIKV nsP2pro active site, which is obtained via molecular docking simulations. In particular, the catalytic residues were denoted as Cys478, Ser482 and His548. Red dashed lines denote Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 pairs. (D) Interaction diagram between CHIKV nsP2pro and NSC 80731 in docking mode, which was prepared using PLIP web application [54]. (E) MD-refined binding pose of NSC 80731 to CHIKV nsP2pro and the pairs (red dashed lines) including Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548. In particular, the MD-refined structure was obtained through clustering methods. (F) Interaction diagram between CHIKV nsP2pro and NSC 80731 in MD-refined binding mode, which was prepared using PLIP web application [54].Five top-lead compounds with the strongest binding affinity to CHIKV nsP2pro are listed in table 1. Besides, RA-0002034 [15], an available inhibitor of nsP2pro, was also docked to the protease for comparison. The obtained result is also mentioned in table 1, in which the docking energy of –9.9 kcal mol–1 is in good agreement with the experimental value, ΔGEXP = −9.27 kcal mol–1. The outcomes imply that mVina is an appropriate protocol for estimating the possible binding compounds to CHIKV nsP2pro. The binding pose between ligands and nsP2pro is shown in figure 2 and figures S1–S6 in the supplementary material. The docking interaction diagrams suggested that three residues—Tyr544, Asn547 and Leu670—may act as important elements during the ligand binding process because they form HB, hydrophobic or π-stacking contacts to CHIKV nsP2pro. The ligands may indirectly alter the pairs including Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548, as they interact rigidly with the residue Asn547. It should be noted that these pairs are associated with the catalytic domain of the enzyme. Molecular docking outcome implies that five top-lead compounds may act as potential inhibitors for CHIKV nsP2pro. Table 1.The ligand binding affinity provided by molecular docking simulations.ano.ligandΔGDockΔGEXPb1NSC 319990–13.32NSC 80731–13.33NSC 80735–13.34NSC 67436–13.15NSC 37553–13.06RA-0002034 –9.9–9.27 [15]aThe unit of energy is kcal mol–1.bThe experimental binding free energy was calculated via formula ΔGEXP = RTln(Ki), where R is the gas constant, T is the absolute temperature, and Ki is the inhibition constant.3.2.Refining docking results with molecular dynamics simulationsIt should be noted that molecular docking simulations commonly use several approximations and constraints to speed up the calculation process [59–61]. The applied simplifications involved using a rigid receptor, using an implicit solvent model, incorporating a united atom model limiting a number of trail binding pose, etc. [35,60,62,63]. Therefore, although the molecular docking simulations provided an appropriate outcome, MD simulations were then carried out to refine the results. The complexes, including CHIKV nsP2pro + NCI compounds, were parametrized and mimicked using MD simulations. Besides, the CHIKV nsP2pro + RA-0002034 was also investigated because RA-0002034 acts as a positive control. The ligand binding pose and nsP2pro structure changed during MD simulations (cf. figures S1–S6 in the supplementary material). In particular, ligands have established highly optimized and stable networks of HBs and hydrophobic interactions with important active-site residues such as Tyr544, Trp549, Asn547 and Ala511. Thus the binding mechanisms were explored based on structural analyses. Each complex was simulated three times in MD simulations with a length of 200 ns. Furthermore, the free ligand in solution was mimicked for over 20 ns of MD simulations. The binding affinity of ligands to CHIKV nsP2pro was clarified using binding free energy protocols [64,65]. Here, perturbation simulations were acquired to complete this task since providing the most accurate results until the date [66,67]. Notably, this method has a proven track record of successful application across numerous biological targets [45,46,68,69,70].The CHIKV nsP2pro + ligand complexes in solution mostly reached equilibrium conditions after ca 100 ns of MD simulations according to the obtained RMSD presented in table S1 in the supplementary material. Moreover, the free ligand in solution also reached stable states after ca 2.5 ns of MD simulations (cf. supplementary material, table S2). The systemic coordinates within the equilibrium intervals were collected for structural analysis. To clarify the binding picture between nsP2pro and inhibitor, the representative conformations of the complexes in solution were estimated using the clustering method over all equilibrium snapshots. A non-hydrogen atom cut-off of 0.3 nm was applied. The ligand interaction diagrams were then investigated using PLIP web application [54]. The outcomes are described in figure 2 and figures S1–S5 in the supplementary material. MD-refined findings suggested that the residues Asn476, Ala511, Tyr512, Tyr544 and Trp549 act as crucial residues controlling the binding process of nsP2pro inhibitors. Although top-leads and the available inhibitor do not form rigid interactions to Cys478 or Ser482 or His548, the six compounds can change the pairs involving Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 via interacting with Asn476 and Trp549. Indeed, the pairs including Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 were significantly changed when the ligands were induced. The outcomes are described in figure 3 and table S3 in the supplementary material. In particular, the average of the spacing between Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 is 7.4 ± 1.4 and 8.9 ± 1.8 Å, respectively, when the free nsP2pro in solution is considered. When the considered inhibitors were induced, the distances of the pair Cys478-Sγ – Nε-His548 are significantly enlarged compared to the ones of the free nsP2pro in solution and nsP2pro + RA-0002034 systems (cf. supplementary material, table S3). Meanwhile, the distance of the pair Ser482-Oγ - Nε-His548 varies depending on the specific ligand (cf. Table S3 of the Supporting Information). The findings suggest that five NCI compounds can prevent the biological activity of nsP2pro. Figure 3.Distribution of the pairs between Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 (upper panel) and Ser482-Oγ–…
full_text_sections.conclusion: 4.ConclusionIn this work, the possible inhibitors for CHIKV nsP2pro were investigated using computational works. In particular, the ligand binding process to nsP2pro, an important enzyme for viral replication, was intensively investigated by combining molecular docking, molecular dynamics and perturbation simulations.The outcomes indicated that five NCI compounds could act as possible agents to inhibit CHIKV nsP2pro. These inhibitors exhibit rigid, non-covalent binding affinities to the viral protease that are significantly larger than those of the available inhibitor RA-0002034. Moreover, MD-refined simulations were then carried out to clarify the binding poses and factors of ligands to nsP2pro. During the equilibrium intervals, the ligands rigidly formed contacts with the residues Asn476, Ala511, Tyr512, Tyr544 and Trp549 of nsP2pro. Furthermore, five NCI compounds probably prevent the biological activity of CHIKV nsP2pro by increasing the distance of the pairs Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548. In addition, ADME estimation confirmed that these top candidates possess excellent human intestinal absorption metrics, identifying them as druggable lead scaffolds and safe.Overall, the findings suggested that five NCI compounds are highly promising candidates for further experimental validation as novel CHIKV nsP2pro inhibitors. However, these findings are based on in silico models; therefore, future in vitro enzymatic and cell-based antiviral assays are fundamentally required to validate the obtained results.
full_text_sections.other: 1.IntroductionChikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an enveloped RNA virus belonging to the genus Alphavirus that causes a viral illness known as chikungunya fever, which is transmitted by mosquitoes [1,2]. Chikungunya fever rapidly spread across 16 countries and territories in the Americas, Africa, Asia and Europe with 240 000 cases and 90 deaths in 2025 [3]. The symptoms include fever, nausea, painful joints, fatigue and a rash [3]. The infection also causes heart damage [3] and influences the quality of life for up to six years [4,5]. The virus was first characterized in the early 1950s [1]. From then until now, this disease has seen multiple recurring outbreaks, yet a cure remains elusive.CHIKV genome includes non-structural protein (nsP) 1 (negative-strand RNA synthesis), nsP2 (helicase and protease activity), nsP3 (RNA synthesis), nsP4 (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase), structural proteins C (capsid), E1-E3 (envelope glycoproteins) and 6K/TF (translation products of the same gene) [1]. Among these, nsP2 is a non-structural and multi-functional protein responsible for cleaving polyproteins into individual functional proteins and unwinding RNA for viral replication [6]. The enzyme includes two domains and one flexible linker. The first domain responds for unwinding viral RNA, a step necessary for replication. This domain also has NTPase and RTPase activity [7]. The methyltransferase-like and protease domain acts as molecular ‘scissors’, cleaving the viral polyproteins into individual functional proteins [8]. Thus, nsP2 becomes an attractive target for drug design [9–11], especially as there is no homologous enzyme, reducing the risk of toxicity.CHIKV non-structural protein 2 protease (nsP2pro) is a flexible cysteine protease that can switch its catalytic mechanism, which poses both challenges and opportunities for drug design. Unlike typical cysteine proteases that rely on a single fixed Cys-His residue, CHIKV nsP2pro can use either a nearby Cys478 or Ser482 to catalyse the reaction [12–14]. Among these, in the primary nucleophile, the Cys478 is activated, which is typical of cysteine proteases. The Cys478 thiol group, after deprotonation by His548, breaks the peptide bond of the viral polyprotein, starting the cleavage process. Besides, if Cys478 is inhibited, Ser482 can take over the nucleophilic role. Ser482 hydroxyl group performs the same role of Cys478 thiol group, allowing the enzyme to remain active. This creates a backup catalytic mechanism. It may be argued that the successful inhibitor is required to be able to block both catalytic mechanisms of CHIKV nsP2pro. In addition, some critical residues of the protein can be listed as Ala475, Asn476, Trp479, Tyr512, Tyr544, Asn547, Trp549, Asn574 and Met707 [8,15].The development of a viral therapy requires significant funding over a prolonged period using conventional approaches [16]. Currently, the application of computational methods to discover new potential inhibitors can significantly reduce the time and cost of drug exploration [17–20]. In particular, the ligand binding free energy can be characterized via atomistic simulations [21–23]. The inhibitory mechanism would then be illuminated within the computational investigation [24,25]. Moreover, several metrics of pharmacology and pharmacokinetics can be rapidly estimated using a web server or protocol [26–28]. Initially, 1581 compounds were docked to the active site of CHIKV nsP2pro. A stronger docking affinity suggests a better potential inhibitor to the protease. The shortlist of these compounds was then refined via intensive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. papers.title_original: Computational identification of potential inhibitors for chikungunya virus nsP2pro

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify potential inhibitors for the chikungunya virus nsP2pro to address the lack of approved therapies for chikungunya virus infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A computational study was conducted using the National Cancer Institute (NCI) database to screen possible inhibitors for nsP2pro, with the focus on the chikungunya virus and its non-structural protein 2 protease.
analysis.methods: Computational approaches including molecular docking simulations with AutoDock Vina, molecular dynamics simulations using GROMACS, and free energy perturbation (FEP) simulations were employed to assess ligand binding affinity and conformational changes.
analysis.main_results: Five compounds, NSC 319990, NSC 80731, NSC 80735, NSC 67436, and NSC 37553, exhibited significantly stronger binding affinity, ranging from –9.70 ± 0.61 to –11.71 ± 1.25 kcal mol–1, compared to the available inhibitor RA-0002034, which had a ΔGFEP of −6.45 ± 0.32 kcal mol–1. The distances of the Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 pair were significantly enlarged when these inhibitors were present.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the stronger binding affinity of these five compounds correlates with their ability to inhibit the biological activity of nsP2pro, suggesting they are promising candidates for further experimental validation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings could inform the development of novel therapeutic strategies targeting nsP2pro, potentially leading to new treatments for chikungunya virus infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its computational nature, which may not fully capture biological complexity. However, the evidence is strong as it is based on rigorous simulations and statistical validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify potential inhibitors for the chikungunya virus nsP2pro due to the lack of approved therapies for chikungunya infections. A computational approach was used to screen ligands from the NCI database, focusing on the chikungunya virus and its nsP2pro structure. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and free energy perturbation simulations were employed to evaluate binding affinity and conformational changes. The results showed that five compounds had significantly stronger binding affinity than the available inhibitor RA-0002034, with the distances of specific residue pairs being enlarged. The authors interpreted that these compounds could inhibit nsP2pro activity, suggesting they are promising candidates for further experimental validation. These findings may inform the development of new treatments for chikungunya virus infections. The study's computational nature limits its biological applicability, but the evidence is strong due to rigorous simulations and statistical validation.

elements_zh.main_results: 五种化合物,NSC 319990、NSC 80731、NSC 80735、NSC 67436和NSC 37553,表现出显著更强的结合亲和力,范围从–9.70 ± 0.61到–11.71 ± 1.25 kcal mol–1,与现有抑制剂RA-0002034相比(其ΔGFEP为−6.45 ± 0.32 kcal mol–1)。当这些抑制剂存在时,Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548对的距离显著增大。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,这五种化合物更强的结合亲和力与其抑制 nsP2pro 生物活性的能力相关,表明它们是有希望进一步实验验证的候选化合物。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为针对 nsP2pro 的新型治疗策略的开发提供信息,从而有可能导致针对 基孔肯雅病毒 感染的新 治疗。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到其计算性质的限制,可能无法完全捕捉生物的复杂性。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它基于严格的模拟和统计验证。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify potential inhibitors for the chikungunya virus nsP2pro to address the lack of approved therapies for chikungunya virus infections.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A computational study was conducted using the National Cancer Institute (NCI) database to screen possible inhibitors for nsP2pro, with the focus on the chikungunya virus and its non-structural protein 2 protease.
analysis_en.methods: Computational approaches including molecular docking simulations with AutoDock Vina, molecular dynamics simulations using GROMACS, and free energy perturbation (FEP) simulations were employed to assess ligand binding affinity and conformational changes.
analysis_en.main_results: Five compounds, NSC 319990, NSC 80731, NSC 80735, NSC 67436, and NSC 37553, exhibited significantly stronger binding affinity, ranging from –9.70 ± 0.61 to –11.71 ± 1.25 kcal mol–1, compared to the available inhibitor RA-0002034, which had a ΔGFEP of −6.45 ± 0.32 kcal mol–1. The distances of the Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 pair were significantly enlarged when these inhibitors were present.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the stronger binding affinity of these five compounds correlates with their ability to inhibit the biological activity of nsP2pro, suggesting they are promising candidates for further experimental validation.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings could inform the development of novel therapeutic strategies targeting nsP2pro, potentially leading to new treatments for chikungunya virus infections.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its computational nature, which may not fully capture biological complexity. However, the evidence is strong as it is based on rigorous simulations and statistical validation.
