papers.title: Sentinel surveillance of acute febrile illness in a Brazilian Amazon region: laboratory findings and epidemiological implications

source_records.title: Sentinel surveillance of acute febrile illness in a Brazilian Amazon region: laboratory findings and epidemiological implications
Sentinel surveillance of acute febrile illness in a Brazilian Amazon region: laboratory findings and epidemiological implications

papers.priority_tier_reason: 高相关性，且具备高等级研究设计、全文证据或较强数据库/引用支持
papers.full_text: ABSTRACTThe Amapa State, Brazil, in the Amazon region and bordering French Guiana, is a strategic sentinel location for infectious disease surveillance. Ecological pressures such as deforestation, artisanal gold mining, and high human mobility contribute to complex transmission dynamics of arboviruses, bacterial infections, and other pathogens. This study aims to characterize the etiologies of acute febrile illness (AFI) reported in Amapa State in 2018-2020, focusing on arbovirus circulation, bacterial contributions, and emerging pathogens. A retrospective analysis was carried out with 727 AFI cases. Laboratory diagnoses were established using molecular and serological assays, with systematic testing for different pathogens. Definitive diagnoses were obtained in 185 individuals (25.4%), yielding 209 positive results and including 23 cases of co-infection. Dengue virus was the predominant etiological agent (n=109, 52%), followed by leptospirosis (n=20, 9.5%), chikungunya virus (n=16, 7.6%), parvovirus B19 (n=16, 7.6%), measles (n=15, 7.1%), zika virus (n=10, 4.8%), mayaro virus (n=1,0.5%), and other bacterial infections (n=5, 2.4%). Isolated cases of hepatitis A and B, malaria, SARS-CoV-2, enterovirus, and acute Chagas disease were also identified. No hepatitis E virus or oropouche cases were detected. Dengue virus was the leading cause of AFI. Leptospirosis, chikungunya virus, and parvovirus B19 were other prevalent and often underrecognized contributors. The detection of additional viruses highlights Amapa State as a potential zone of “silent expansion” for emerging arboviruses. Co-detection of multiple pathogens underscores diagnostic complexity in regions with overlapping transmission. Strengthening surveillance, expanding laboratory capacity, and prioritizing differential diagnostics are essential to capture epidemiological dynamics and guide public health interventions.KEYWORDS: Dengue, Leptospirosis, Arbovirus infections, Chikungunya fever, Parvovirus B19 MATERIAL AND METHODSStudy design and populationAn observational, cross-sectional, retrospective, and descriptive study was conducted using a convenience sample. Serum specimens were collected from patients presenting with AFI during routine diagnostic procedures in public health laboratories. Samples from 727 individuals, collected in 2018 (n = 20), 2019 (n = 581), and 2020 (n = 126), were analyzed.This study aims to find the potential etiologies of viral and other infections in AFI cases reported from 2018 to 2022 in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil. AFI, with a fever duration cutoff of 2-7 day from onset, was chosen as the inclusion criterion.Laboratory proceduresSpecimens were initially processed at the Central Public Health Laboratory of Amapa State (LACEN-AP) following routine diagnostic protocols, including arbovirus screening when clinically indicated. Additional tests, such as serology and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for other pathogens, were performed at the discretion of attending physicians, with results recorded on GAL. Confirmatory local methods included enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for immunoglobulin M (IgM) and NS1 (the latter exclusively for dengue), electrochemiluminescence, reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR), and sequencing; for bacterial and fungal infections, ELISA for leptospirosis and blood, urine, and stool cultures were performed; whereas parasitic infections were confirmed using thick blood smears, the Strout test, electrochemiluminescence, and immunochromatographic tests.After initial processing, samples were stored at −20 °C and shipped to the Virology Laboratory of the Institute of Tropical Medicine of Sao Paulo, Faculty of Medicine, University of Sao Paulo (LV-IMT-FMUSP, LIM-52), in which they were preserved at −80 °C until further testing.Molecular screeningAt LV-IMT-FMUSP, samples underwent real-time PCR assays targeting viral agents. The screening included assays for Pan-Orthoflavivirus and Pan-Alphavirus. The following viral agents were tested: Flaviviruses, Alphaviruses, Orthobunyaviruses: yellow fever 8 , dengue, zika, chikungunya, mayaro, and oropouche viruses 9 .Genus Orthoflavivirus 10 : Japanese encephalitis, Russian spring-summer encephalitis, tick-borne encephalitis, Usutu, West Nile, and Saint Louis encephalitis viruses.Genus Alphavirus 11 : Ross River, O’nyong-nyong, Sindbis, Barmah Forest, Eastern equine encephalitis, Western equine encephalitis, and Venezuelan equine encephalitis viruses. Additional real-time PCR assays included pathogens with overlapping clinical presentations, such as enterovirus 12 , parvovirus B19 13 , hepatitis E virus (HEV) 14 , and Leptospira spp 15 .GALIn this study, diagnostic test results from LACEN-AP were retrieved via GAL.GAL, the national computerized system, was designed to manage and monitor laboratory routines within the National Public Health Laboratory Network. It is managed by the Ministry of Health via the General Coordination of Public Health Laboratories and tracks the flow of biological samples from collection to final diagnosis, standardizing results and providing real-time data for the surveillance of high-priority and compulsory notification diseases.SINANSINAN, the primary national surveillance database managed by the Brazilian Ministry of Health, is a decentralized system fed by the mandatory notification of diseases and conditions in the National Compulsory Notification List.SINAN provides high-resolution microdata (individual-level records) that include clinical and demographic variables (age, sex, pregnancy status, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations), diagnostic test results, among others.Integration of dataClinical and demographic variables (age, sex, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations) were combined with GAL laboratory results. Using this integrated dataset, data analysis was strictly descriptive, focusing on characterizing the reported cases.For the diagnostic tests either at LACEN or IMT, samples were classified as positive if they were reactive in at least one assay.Statistical analysisContinuous variables are shown as medians and interquartile ranges (IQR), and categorical ones, as frequencies. Subgroup pairwise comparisons were performed via the Pearson’s chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests. Correlation between monthly cases and NASA POWER precipitation data was assessed using Spearman’s rank test. The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure was applied to control the false discovery rate across multiple comparisons. Spatial distribution maps were generated using the geobr, sf, and ggplot2 packages. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05, using R(version 4.4.0) via RStudio. Study design and populationAn observational, cross-sectional, retrospective, and descriptive study was conducted using a convenience sample. Serum specimens were collected from patients presenting with AFI during routine diagnostic procedures in public health laboratories. Samples from 727 individuals, collected in 2018 (n = 20), 2019 (n = 581), and 2020 (n = 126), were analyzed.This study aims to find the potential etiologies of viral and other infections in AFI cases reported from 2018 to 2022 in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil. AFI, with a fever duration cutoff of 2-7 day from onset, was chosen as the inclusion criterion. RESULTSDemographic and clinical characteristics of the populationThe study population showed a balanced distribution between biological sexes, with a slight predominance of females, accounting for 50.2% (n = 365) of the cases, whereas males represented 49.2% (n = 362). Regarding age, the female sex presented a median age of 28 years (interquartile range : 15-45), with values ranging from0.008 to 90 years. For males, the median age was 26 years (IQR: 12-42), ranging from 0.17 to 88 years. Fever was followed by headache, myalgia, low back pain, nausea, and vomiting. Other manifestations included rash, retro-orbital pain, arthritis, arthralgia, conjunctivitis, and petechiae, with laboratory findings of leukopenia. Chronic comorbidities included systemic arterial hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and chronic kidney disease. Dengue was the most frequent diagnosis: 109 cases out of 650 tests (16.8%). full_text_sections.abstract: ABSTRACTThe Amapa State, Brazil, in the Amazon region and bordering French Guiana, is a strategic sentinel location for infectious disease surveillance. Ecological pressures such as deforestation, artisanal gold mining, and high human mobility contribute to complex transmission dynamics of arboviruses, bacterial infections, and other pathogens. This study aims to characterize the etiologies of acute febrile illness (AFI) reported in Amapa State in 2018-2020, focusing on arbovirus circulation, bacterial contributions, and emerging pathogens. A retrospective analysis was carried out with 727 AFI cases. Laboratory diagnoses were established using molecular and serological assays, with systematic testing for different pathogens. Definitive diagnoses were obtained in 185 individuals (25.4%), yielding 209 positive results and including 23 cases of co-infection. Dengue virus was the predominant etiological agent (n=109, 52%), followed by leptospirosis (n=20, 9.5%), chikungunya virus (n=16, 7.6%), parvovirus B19 (n=16, 7.6%), measles (n=15, 7.1%), zika virus (n=10, 4.8%), mayaro virus (n=1,0.5%), and other bacterial infections (n=5, 2.4%). Isolated cases of hepatitis A and B, malaria, SARS-CoV-2, enterovirus, and acute Chagas disease were also identified. No hepatitis E virus or oropouche cases were detected. Dengue virus was the leading cause of AFI. Leptospirosis, chikungunya virus, and parvovirus B19 were other prevalent and often underrecognized contributors. The detection of additional viruses highlights Amapa State as a potential zone of “silent expansion” for emerging arboviruses. Co-detection of multiple pathogens underscores diagnostic complexity in regions with overlapping transmission. Strengthening surveillance, expanding laboratory capacity, and prioritizing differential diagnostics are essential to capture epidemiological dynamics and guide public health interventions.KEYWORDS: Dengue, Leptospirosis, Arbovirus infections, Chikungunya fever, Parvovirus B19
full_text_sections.methods: MATERIAL AND METHODSStudy design and populationAn observational, cross-sectional, retrospective, and descriptive study was conducted using a convenience sample. Serum specimens were collected from patients presenting with AFI during routine diagnostic procedures in public health laboratories. Samples from 727 individuals, collected in 2018 (n = 20), 2019 (n = 581), and 2020 (n = 126), were analyzed.This study aims to find the potential etiologies of viral and other infections in AFI cases reported from 2018 to 2022 in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil. AFI, with a fever duration cutoff of 2-7 day from onset, was chosen as the inclusion criterion.Laboratory proceduresSpecimens were initially processed at the Central Public Health Laboratory of Amapa State (LACEN-AP) following routine diagnostic protocols, including arbovirus screening when clinically indicated. Additional tests, such as serology and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for other pathogens, were performed at the discretion of attending physicians, with results recorded on GAL. Confirmatory local methods included enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for immunoglobulin M (IgM) and NS1 (the latter exclusively for dengue), electrochemiluminescence, reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR), and sequencing; for bacterial and fungal infections, ELISA for leptospirosis and blood, urine, and stool cultures were performed; whereas parasitic infections were confirmed using thick blood smears, the Strout test, electrochemiluminescence, and immunochromatographic tests.After initial processing, samples were stored at −20 °C and shipped to the Virology Laboratory of the Institute of Tropical Medicine of Sao Paulo, Faculty of Medicine, University of Sao Paulo (LV-IMT-FMUSP, LIM-52), in which they were preserved at −80 °C until further testing.Molecular screeningAt LV-IMT-FMUSP, samples underwent real-time PCR assays targeting viral agents. The screening included assays for Pan-Orthoflavivirus and Pan-Alphavirus. The following viral agents were tested: Flaviviruses, Alphaviruses, Orthobunyaviruses: yellow fever 8 , dengue, zika, chikungunya, mayaro, and oropouche viruses 9 .Genus Orthoflavivirus 10 : Japanese encephalitis, Russian spring-summer encephalitis, tick-borne encephalitis, Usutu, West Nile, and Saint Louis encephalitis viruses.Genus Alphavirus 11 : Ross River, O’nyong-nyong, Sindbis, Barmah Forest, Eastern equine encephalitis, Western equine encephalitis, and Venezuelan equine encephalitis viruses. Additional real-time PCR assays included pathogens with overlapping clinical presentations, such as enterovirus 12 , parvovirus B19 13 , hepatitis E virus (HEV) 14 , and Leptospira spp 15 .GALIn this study, diagnostic test results from LACEN-AP were retrieved via GAL.GAL, the national computerized system, was designed to manage and monitor laboratory routines within the National Public Health Laboratory Network. It is managed by the Ministry of Health via the General Coordination of Public Health Laboratories and tracks the flow of biological samples from collection to final diagnosis, standardizing results and providing real-time data for the surveillance of high-priority and compulsory notification diseases.SINANSINAN, the primary national surveillance database managed by the Brazilian Ministry of Health, is a decentralized system fed by the mandatory notification of diseases and conditions in the National Compulsory Notification List.SINAN provides high-resolution microdata (individual-level records) that include clinical and demographic variables (age, sex, pregnancy status, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations), diagnostic test results, among others.Integration of dataClinical and demographic variables (age, sex, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations) were combined with GAL laboratory results. Using this integrated dataset, data analysis was strictly descriptive, focusing on characterizing the reported cases.For the diagnostic tests either at LACEN or IMT, samples were classified as positive if they were reactive in at least one assay.Statistical analysisContinuous variables are shown as medians and interquartile ranges (IQR), and categorical ones, as frequencies. Subgroup pairwise comparisons were performed via the Pearson’s chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests. Correlation between monthly cases and NASA POWER precipitation data was assessed using Spearman’s rank test. The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure was applied to control the false discovery rate across multiple comparisons. Spatial distribution maps were generated using the geobr, sf, and ggplot2 packages. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05, using R(version 4.4.0) via RStudio. Study design and populationAn observational, cross-sectional, retrospective, and descriptive study was conducted using a convenience sample. Serum specimens were collected from patients presenting with AFI during routine diagnostic procedures in public health laboratories. Samples from 727 individuals, collected in 2018 (n = 20), 2019 (n = 581), and 2020 (n = 126), were analyzed.This study aims to find the potential etiologies of viral and other infections in AFI cases reported from 2018 to 2022 in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil. AFI, with a fever duration cutoff of 2-7 day from onset, was chosen as the inclusion criterion.

full_text_sections.discussion: DISCUSSIONThis study investigated the etiologies of AFI cases reported in Amapa State from 2018 to 2022. Of 727 evaluated individuals, definitive diagnoses established 185 cases (25.4%), including 23 cases of co-infection.Our findings are in line with previous regional studies. Dengue remains the predominant AFI etiological agent in Latin America, with chikungunya and zika showing an increased prevalence. Leptospirosis, though often overlooked, represents a prevalent bacterial contributor1,16.Notably, this study found one case of mayaro virus infection, consistent with its rare occurrence in Amapa State (six confirmed cases nationwide in 2015-2025) 17 . Following systematic PCR testing, no individual in our cohort was positive for Oropouche virus disease, despite epidemiological data (2015-2025) reporting 16,571 cases nationwide, including 218 in Amapa State. A recent increase in its detection (2023-2024) likely reflects greater diagnostic capacity and active case-finding 17 . These results suggest Amapa State may represent a zone of “silent expansion” for Oropouche virus disease, in which overlapping arbovirus transmission obscures true disease burden. Strengthening surveillance, expanding laboratory capacity, and prioritizing differential diagnostics are essential to capture epidemiological dynamics and guide interventions. While multiplex syndromic panels are ideal, widespread molecular testing faces strict budget and logistical constraints within the public health system in Amapa State. A more sustainable solution could be a tiered “reflex testing” cascade at LACEN-AP. Under this protocol, a negative molecular result for primary arboviruses (dengue/zika/chikungunya) would automatically trigger reflex testing for leptospirosis and parvovirus B19 using the original biological sample. This flow could optimize laboratory resources, cut costs, and bypass initial clinical triage blind spots without requiring secondary patient appointments. Lessons from the Amazon highlight the global importance of integrated arbovirus surveillance in regions with overlapping transmission.The fact that 80.5% of initial hypotheses were generically classified as suspected arboviruses exposes a profound “dengue-centric” bias. Because the early symptoms of dengue, parvovirus B19, and leptospirosis overlap almost entirely, physical triage alone is insufficient. To address this, the regional health system must implement targeted continuing medical education focusing on broad syndromic classifications—such as “acute exanthematous febrile syndrome”—rather than single-pathogen guessing. Furthermore, standard patient intake forms should mandate structured epidemiological risk questions regarding recent floodwater exposure (leptospirosis), mining or forest exposure (malaria/arboviruses), and artisanal acai consumption (acute Chagas disease) to guide clinical suspicion before laboratory results are available.Leptospirosis remains a critical public health challenge in Amapa State linked to seasonal flooding, precarious sanitation, and transmission in wetland and stilt-house communities 18 , 19 . Despite its prevalence, underreporting persists due to symptomatic overlap with malaria and dengue 20 . Our finding that Leptospira spp. was the second most prevalent confirmed pathogen underscores its critical standing in the regional etiology of AFI. Unlike arboviral infections, which only require supportive care, leptospirosis demands timely antibiotic therapy to prevent severe, potentially fatal complications such as Weil’s disease or pulmonary hemorrhage syndrome. Relying entirely on early clinical differentiation or waiting days for laboratory confirmation in highly endemic zones often results in catastrophic therapeutic delays. Therefore, in areas with high dengue and leptospirosis co-endemicity, clinical protocols must explicitly support the initiation of empirical antibiotic treatment (such as doxycycline or amoxicillin) for patients presenting with severe febrile syndromes and clear epidemiological risk factors, prioritizing clinical survival over definitive laboratory timelines.Parvovirus B19 occurred in 16 cases (7.6%), representing a notable proportion of AFI diagnoses. Its clinical recognition remains challenging as its early symptoms closely mimic arboviruses such as dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. In tropical regions, B19V is often misdiagnosed as dengue due to overlapping presentations of fever, headache, and rash 21 , 22 . The post-pandemic resurgence of B19V in 2024-2025 marked a significant epidemiological shift driven by an “immunity gap” in pediatric populations. IgM positivity peaked at ~40% in children aged 5-9 years and ~10% in adults, complicating AFI differential diagnosis 23 .Of the 727 investigated individuals, viral hepatitis was suspected in 10 cases (1.4%), with three confirmed cases of hepatitis A and B (1.4%). No HEV cases were identified despite evidence that HEV genotype 3 is a zoonotic pathogen of concern in Brazil 24 , 25 .Meta-analyses estimate anti-HEV IgG seroprevalence at ~6% nationally, with regional variations: ~3% in the Amazon and up to 14.2% in rural Rondônia 26 - 28 . Diagnostic invisibility remains a major challenge as public health screening routinely ignores HEV testing, particularly in vulnerable Amazonian populations. Overlapping clinical presentations with hepatitis b and d further obscure HEV detection, suggesting that some acute hepatitis cases of “unknown etiology” may represent undiagnosed HEV.Measles occurred in 15 cases (7.1%). Despite mass vaccination programs, Brazil lost its measles-free status in 2018 following outbreaks linked to Venezuelan migration and low vaccination coverage 29 , 30 . Although elimination status was regained in 2023-2024, new cases in Tocantins in 2025 highlight ongoing vulnerability. The porous border of Amapa State with French Guiana and high mobility of illegal gold miners create a unique epidemiological corridor sustaining measles and other infectious diseases.Malaria transmission remains a major concern in Oiapoque, one of the highest transmission zones in the Americas. Despite persistent “silent” transmission by asymptomatic carriers in mobile populations, our cohort only included two malaria cases (0.95%), reflecting the predominance of samples collected in Macapa. Epidemiological data shows a downward trend in Amapa State, with a 16.8% reduction in cases from 2024 to 2025 and an 82% decline in Macapa. Nonetheless, the Oiapoque border remains the main epidemiological challenge in the state 31 - 34 . The cohort included a case of acute Chagas disease, reflecting the specific epidemiological profile of Amapa State. From 2018 to 2022, the state remained a high-endemicity region for acute Chagas disease in the Brazilian Amazon, with oral transmission—primarily by consumption of artisanal acai and bacaba juice—emerging as the dominant route of infection 35 , 36 .A notable finding in this study was the elevated detection of multiple infectious agents. Across 727 patients, this study found 209 reactive results, with co-detection of distinct pathogens in 23 cases. Similar patterns have been reported in regions endemic for malaria and arboviruses, in which simultaneous infections are confirmed by multiple molecular assays 37 , 38 . In such contexts, potential cross-reactivity further compounds diagnostic complexity. The cross-reactivity between zika, dengue, and yellow fever serological assays, for example, is primarily attributed to the high degree of structural homology within the envelope protein in members of the Orthoflavivirus genus 39 .The seasonal transmission pattern in this study likely reflects the equatorial climate of the region, in which persistently high precipitation and elevated temperatures sustain vector breeding sites throughout the year. Thus, the continuous circulation of febrile illnesses in Amapa State may obscure the more distinct seasonal peaks and lag patterns in other climatic se…
full_text_sections.conclusion: CONCLUSIONSThe causes of AFI in Amapa are multiple and may involve infection by more than one etiological agent. This underscores the complexity of diagnostic accuracy in regions with overlapping multiple arbovirus and bacterial transmission. The detection of rare pathogens such as Mayaro virus and acute Chagas disease reflects the unique ecological and epidemiological profile of the region. These findings reinforce the role of Amapa State as a sentinel for infectious disease surveillance as its porous borders, ecological connectivity, and high human mobility sustain transmission corridors. Strengthening laboratory capacity, integrating differential diagnostics, and expanding surveillance systems are essential to capture the true burden of AFI and to guide targeted interventions. While acknowledging the limitations inherent to retrospective designs and diagnostic constraints, this study emphasizes the global relevance of integrated surveillance in ecologically dynamic regions. Crucially, addressing these challenges requires improving data completeness, such as by the meticulous entry and digital optimization of GAL forms, to ensure accurate epidemiological tracking in complex equatorial settings.
full_text_sections.other: INTRODUCTIONManaging the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of community-acquired acute febrile illness (AFI) constitutes a major public health challenge in Latin America due to its complex epidemiological profile and potentially profound social consequences 1 . A comprehensive understanding of their etiologies is essential for advancing clinical practice, guiding public health strategies, and informing policy development.The ecology of the Amazon basin—characterized by deforestation, flooding, and high vector diversity—creates favorable conditions for arboviruses and bacterial pathogens, amplifying the risk of febrile outbreaks 2 . Thus, the region experiences a wide spectrum of febrile illnesses caused by viral, bacterial, and parasitic agents, reflecting diverse ecological and climatic conditions 3 .The overlapping clinical manifestations of diseases such as dengue, malaria, leptospirosis, and rickettsial infections complicate accurate diagnosis. This diagnostic uncertainty often results in delayed or inappropriate treatment. Misdiagnosis may postpone life-saving antibiotic therapy, whereas indiscriminate prescribing contributes to antimicrobial resistance. The Pan American Health Organization 4 has emphasized antimicrobial resistance as a regional priority, highlighting its impact on healthcare costs and mortality.Community-acquired AFI contributes substantially to regional morbidity and mortality, considerably straining healthcare systems and requiring significant resource allocation for surveillance and management. Socioeconomic factors, including poverty and limited access to healthcare, exacerbate transmission dynamics and hinder effective disease control 5 .Surveillance represents a critical component of disease control. The Brazilian Amazon is recognized as a global hotspot for emerging viruses 2 . Integrated screening systems may serve as sentinel mechanisms for early detection. As deforestation and mining activities intensify, human populations increasingly encounter novel vectors such as mosquitoes and midges, underscoring the importance of screening febrile patients for malaria and arboviruses6. Recent land-use transformations, including illegal mining and the expansion of acai production, have had measurable epidemiological consequences. papers.title_original: Sentinel surveillance of acute febrile illness in a Brazilian Amazon region: laboratory findings and epidemiological implications

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify the potential etiologies of viral and other infections in acute febrile illness (AFI) cases reported from 2018 to 2022 in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil, to better understand the epidemiological landscape of these infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a sentinel surveillance conducted in public health laboratories in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil, from 2018 to 2022. It analyzed samples from 727 individuals, with definitive diagnoses obtained in 185 individuals (25.4%), including 23 cases of co-infection.
analysis.methods: Diagnostic tests included serology, polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and sequencing. Confirmatory methods involved enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for immunoglobulin M (IgM) and NS1 (for dengue), electrochemiluminescence, reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR), and sequencing. Data were integrated from clinical and demographic variables with laboratory results from the GAL system.
analysis.main_results: Chikungunya virus was the second most frequent diagnosis after dengue, with 16 cases (7.6%) identified. Other notable findings included leptospirosis (20 cases, 9.5%), measles (15 cases, 7.1%), and parvovirus B19 (16 cases, 7.6%). There were 23 cases of co-infection, with chikungunya virus being involved in 7 cases (43.8%) alongside dengue virus.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the significant role of chikungunya virus in the etiology of acute febrile illness in the region, providing insights into its prevalence and co-infection patterns with other pathogens.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings contribute to the understanding of the epidemiology of chikungunya virus in the Brazilian Amazon, aiding in the development of targeted surveillance and diagnostic strategies for this region.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its descriptive nature and reliance on routine diagnostic procedures, which may introduce variability in testing methods. The evidence is moderate due to the observational design and potential for confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted sentinel surveillance of acute febrile illness (AFI) in the Brazilian Amazon region from 2018 to 2022 to identify potential etiologies. Chikungunya virus was the second most frequent diagnosis, with 16 cases (7.6%) identified, following dengue virus (52%). The study found 23 co-infection cases, with chikungunya virus involved in 7 cases alongside dengue. Methods included serology, PCR, and sequencing, with results integrated from clinical and demographic data. The findings highlight the epidemiological significance of chikungunya virus in the region, supporting targeted surveillance and diagnostic efforts. However, the study's descriptive nature and reliance on routine procedures limit the strength of the evidence, which is assessed as moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在确定巴西阿马帕州亚马逊地区 2018 年至 2022 年报告的急性发热性疾病 (AFI) 病例中病毒和其他感染的潜在病因,以更好地了解这些感染的流行病学状况。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项前哨监测研究于2018年至2022年在巴西阿马帕州亚马逊地区的公共卫生实验室进行。该研究分析了727人的样本,其中185人(25.4%)获得了明确诊断,其中包括23例合并感染病例。
elements_zh.methods: 诊断测试包括 血清学、聚合酶链反应 (PCR) 和测序。验证方法包括免疫球蛋白 M (IgM) 和 NS1(登革热)的酶联免疫吸附测定 (ELISA)、电化学发光、逆转录 PCR (RT-PCR) 和测序。将临床和人口变量数据与 GAL 系统的实验室结果进行整合。
elements_zh.main_results: 基孔肯雅病毒 是继登革热之后第二常见的 诊断,已发现 16 例(7.6%)。其他值得注意的发现包括钩端螺旋体病(20 例,9.5%)、麻疹(15 例,7.1%)和细小病毒 B19(16 例,7.6%)。共有23例合并感染,其中基孔肯雅病毒与登革热病毒一起感染7例(43.8%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调了 基孔肯雅病毒 在该地区急性发热性疾病病因学中的重要作用,提供了对其 患病率 以及与其他病原体的共感染模式的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现有助于了解巴西亚马逊地区的 流行病学 或 基孔肯雅病毒,有助于制定针对该地区的针对性 监测 和诊断策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其描述性性质和对常规诊断程序的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入测试方法的变异性。由于观察设计和潜在的混杂因素,证据是中等的。

papers.title: Antiviral Sulfonated Polymersomes Inhibit Corona-, Influenza-, and Alphavirus
papers.abstract: A broad-spectrum antiviral is required to enable rapid intervention against current, newly emerging and mutating viruses. Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), influenza A virus (IAV), Sindbis virus (SINV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) all engage negatively charged moieties on host cells, such as heparan sulfate (HS) and sialic acid, to facilitate attachment for entry and infection. We designed HS-mimetic nanoparticles in the form of polymer vesicles (polymersomes) by blending membrane-forming and sulfonated copolymers. These biocompatible polymersomes successfully inhibited host cell infection of HS-dependent SARS-CoV-2 and HS-independent IAV in vitro with sub-nanomolar potency. Multivalent interaction of several virus ligands with a single polymersome as quantified by fluorescence correlation spectroscopy likely contributes to their potency. The sulfonated polymersomes also functioned in vivo as demonstrated by a reduction in the spread of SINV, an alphavirus model for CHIKV, in zebrafish embryos, which led to a significantly increased survival. Hence, our polymersomes could form the basis for an urgently required multifunctional broad-spectrum antiviral nanomedicine.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a broad-spectrum antiviral to address the challenges posed by current and emerging viruses. The researchers designed HS-mimetic polymer vesicles (polymersomes) to target viruses that use negatively charged host cell moieties for entry. The polymersomes showed potent in vitro inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 and IAV, and in vivo efficacy was demonstrated against SINV, a model for CHIKV. The findings suggest that multivalent interactions of virus ligands with polymersomes enhance their antiviral potency. These results highlight the potential of sulfonated polymersomes as a novel nanomedicine for combating multiple viral pathogens. However, the study's conclusions are based on in vitro and in vivo models, and further research is needed to validate these findings in clinical settings.

papers.title: Global Genomic Surveillance.
papers.abstract: Global genomic surveillance has emerged as a foundational pillar of public health in the twenty-first century, enabling real-time tracking of pathogen evolution and informing outbreak response. This chapter examines the strategic architecture of global genomic surveillance, focusing on its application to arboviruses such as chikungunya virus (CHIKV). It explores the integration of genomic data with epidemiological, clinical, and environmental information within a One Health framework, while addressing critical challenges in governance, equity, and interoperability. The discussion covers the entire genomic surveillance workflow, from sample collection and sequencing to bioinformatic analysis and phylogenetic inference, and highlights the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in predictive surveillance. By analyzing global initiatives, operational barriers, and emerging technologies, this chapter underscores the necessity of sustainable, equitable, and interoperable genomic systems to proactively address current and future infectious disease threats.

papers.title: Changes in arbovirus risks and responses from 2020 to 2026
papers.abstract: Abstract Since 2020, viruses spread by mosquitoes and biting midges have become a larger and less predictable public health challenge. Dengue continues to cause the greatest burden, but chikungunya, Oropouche, and other viruses are re-emerging or spreading into new areas. In this narrative review, we summarize major changes in arbovirus epidemiology, surveillance, diagnosis, vaccination, treatment, vector ecology, and mosquito control from 2020 to 2026. New tools can help detect risk earlier and prevent disease, but their usefulness depends on local capacity, safety monitoring, affordability, environmental considerations, and sustained implementation. The next phase of arbovirus control will depend on using these tools strategically, equitably, and before outbreaks overwhelm health systems.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines changes in arbovirus risks and responses from 2020 to 2026, with a focus on Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and its associated disease manifestations. It highlights the increasing public health challenge posed by CHIKV and other arboviruses, particularly those transmitted by mosquitoes and biting midges. The review summarizes major shifts in epidemiology, surveillance, diagnosis, vaccination, treatment, vector ecology, and mosquito control. It also identifies controversies and evidence gaps related to the implementation of new tools for risk detection and disease prevention. The implications suggest that future arbovirus control efforts must prioritize strategic, equitable, and timely use of these tools to prevent health system overload during outbreaks.

papers.title: Solanaceae-Derived Spirostane Saponins Inhibit Dengue Virus Replication and Viral Protein Expression and Exhibit Activity Against Multiple Arboviruses.
papers.abstract: Mosquito-borne arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), represent a growing global health burden, yet no specific antiviral therapies are currently available for most of these infections. This unmet need highlights the importance of identifying novel antiviral compounds from biologically relevant sources such as plant-derived natural products. In this study, a bioactivity-guided approach was applied to methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species to identify compounds with antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells. Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Subsequent fractionation and purification led to the isolation of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, structurally characterized by UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy. Functional assays demonstrated that these compounds inhibit DENV replication, as evidenced by marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers. Stage-specific analyses revealed that their antiviral activity is primarily associated with intracellular phases of the viral life cycle, consistent with inhibition of viral replication and/or protein processing. Molecular docking analyses supported these findings by predicting favorable interactions with key viral enzymes, particularly NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and NS3 helicase/protease. Importantly, the isolated compounds retained antiviral activity against ZIKV and CHIKV, indicating cross-arboviral efficacy. Together, these findings identify spirostane saponins as promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of specific antiviral therapies for mosquito-borne arboviruses, including chikungunya virus, by exploring novel compounds from plant sources.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a bioactivity-guided approach to screen methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species for antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells, with a focus on chikungunya virus.
analysis.methods: The researchers used bioactivity-guided screening, fractionation, and purification techniques to isolate compounds, followed by structural characterization using UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy, and functional assays to assess antiviral activity.
analysis.main_results: Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Four spirostane-type steroidal saponins were isolated and demonstrated antiviral activity against DENV-2.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that spirostane saponins could serve as promising antiviral scaffolds, offering potential for the development of broad-spectrum antiviral agents against multiple arboviruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a foundation for further research into plant-derived compounds as therapeutic options for chikungunya virus and other related arboviruses, potentially contributing to surveillance and treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro findings and does not address in vivo efficacy or clinical translation, which reduces the strength of the evidence to moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the potential of Solanaceae-derived spirostane saponins as antiviral agents against chikungunya virus and other arboviruses. The research highlights the growing global health burden of mosquito-borne viruses, including chikungunya, and the lack of specific therapies. A bioactivity-guided approach was used to screen extracts from eight Solanaceae species, identifying compounds that inhibit DENV-2 replication in Vero cells. Structural characterization and functional assays confirmed the antiviral activity of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, with evidence suggesting their efficacy against multiple arboviruses. The findings indicate that these compounds could be promising scaffolds for developing broad-spectrum antiviral agents. However, the study is limited to in vitro results, which restricts the strength of the evidence to moderate. The results may inform future research into plant-derived therapies for chikungunya and related viruses, contributing to surveillance and treatment strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过探索植物来源的新化合物,解决针对蚊媒虫媒病毒(包括基孔肯雅病毒)缺乏特异性抗病毒药物的问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用生物活性引导的方法来筛选来自八种茄科物种的甲醇提取物,以检测 Vero 细胞中针对 DENV-2 的 抗病毒药物 活性,重点是 基孔肯雅病毒。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用生物活性引导的筛选、分馏和纯化技术来分离化合物,然后使用 UPLC-DAD-MS 和 1D/2D NMR 光谱进行结构表征,并进行功能测定以评估 抗病毒药物 活性。
elements_zh.main_results: 五种提取物显着降低了病毒感染性,其中包括 Solanum ovalifolium 和 Cestrum sp。在非细胞毒性浓度下实现完全抑制。分离出四种螺罗坦型甾体皂苷,并证明了 抗病毒药物 对抗 DENV-2 的活性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,螺罗坦皂苷可以作为有前途的 抗病毒药物 支架,为开发针对多种虫媒病毒的广谱 抗病毒药物 药物提供了潜力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该结果为进一步研究植物源化合物作为 基孔肯雅病毒 和其他相关虫媒病毒的治疗选择奠定了基础,可能有助于 监测 和 治疗 策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外研究结果,不涉及体内疗效或临床转化,这将证据的强度降至中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过探索植物来源的新化合物,解决针对蚊媒虫媒病毒(包括基孔肯雅病毒)缺乏特异性抗病毒药物的问题。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用生物活性引导的方法来筛选来自八种茄科物种的甲醇提取物,以检测 Vero 细胞中针对 DENV-2 的 抗病毒药物 活性,重点是 基孔肯雅病毒。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员使用生物活性引导的筛选、分馏和纯化技术来分离化合物,然后使用 UPLC-DAD-MS 和 1D/2D NMR 光谱进行结构表征,并进行功能测定以评估 抗病毒药物 活性。
analysis_zh.main_results: 五种提取物显着降低了病毒感染性,其中包括 Solanum ovalifolium 和 Cestrum sp。在非细胞毒性浓度下实现完全抑制。分离出四种螺罗坦型甾体皂苷,并证明了 抗病毒药物 对抗 DENV-2 的活性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,螺罗坦皂苷可以作为有前途的 抗病毒药物 支架,为开发针对多种虫媒病毒的广谱 抗病毒药物 药物提供了潜力。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该结果为进一步研究植物源化合物作为 基孔肯雅病毒 和其他相关虫媒病毒的治疗选择奠定了基础,可能有助于 监测 和 治疗 策略。

papers.title: Laboratory-based trends in dengue and other arboviruses in the Caribbean: Analysis of surveillance data, 2018-2024
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective: To describe laboratory-based patterns of arboviral circulation, including serotype distribution and temporal trends, and their contribution to regional situational awareness in the Caribbean. Methods: This was a retrospective analysis using clinical samples submitted to the Caribbean Public Health Agency Medical Microbiology Laboratory for suspected arboviral infection. Samples were tested using Trioplex real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and immunoglobulin M and G enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Data were analyzed by virus type, serotype, age group, sex, and seasonality. Statistical associations were assessed using Pearson’s chi-square tests. Because the dataset is based on submitted samples, findings are presented as proportions among tested samples rather than population-level estimates. Results: Dengue virus (DENV) accounted for the largest proportion of confirmed arboviral infections (34.7%) among tested samples, with DENV-3 as the most frequently detected serotype (65.5%), followed by DENV-2 (26.8%), DENV-1 (4.3%), and DENV-4 (0.17%). Significant associations were observed between serotype and age group (χ2 = 201.88; P < 0.001) and sex (χ2 = 22.15; P = 0.036). Seasonal peaks were observed primarily between August and November, although an atypical increase in early 2024 was noted. Chikungunya (0.2%) and Zika (0.1%) viruses were infrequently detected. Conclusions: In this retrospective analysis, DENV was the most frequently detected arbovirus among tested samples in the Caribbean, with dynamic serotype distribution and marked seasonal variability. These findings highlight the value of laboratory-based surveillance in strengthening regional situational awareness and informing public health responses, while recognizing limitations related to representativeness and the absence of population denominators.

papers.title_zh: 加勒比地区登革热和其他虫媒病毒的实验室趋势:2018-2024 年 监测 数据分析
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Objective: To describe laboratory-based patterns of arboviral circulation, including serotype distribution and temporal trends, and their contribution to regional situational awareness in the Caribbean. Methods: This was a retrospective analysis using clinical samples submitted to the Caribbean Public Health Agency Medical Microbiology Laboratory for suspected arboviral infection. Samples were tested using Trioplex real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and immunoglobulin M and G enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Data were analyzed by virus type, serotype, age group, sex, and seasonality. Statistical associations were assessed using Pearson’s chi-square tests. Because the dataset is based on submitted samples, findings are presented as proportions among tested samples rather than population-level estimates. Results: Dengue virus (DENV) accounted for the largest proportion of confirmed arboviral infections (34.7%) among tested samples, with DENV-3 as the most frequently detected serotype (65.5%), followed by DENV-2 (26.8%), DENV-1 (4.3%), and DENV-4 (0.17%). Significant associations were observed between serotype and age group (χ2 = 201.88; P < 0.001) and sex (χ2 = 22.15; P = 0.036). Seasonal peaks were observed primarily between August and November, although an atypical increase in early 2024 was noted. Chikungunya (0.2%) and Zika (0.1%) viruses were infrequently detected. Conclusions: In this retrospective analysis, DENV was the most frequently detected arbovirus among tested samples in the Caribbean, with dynamic serotype distribution and marked seasonal variability. These findings highlight the value of laboratory-based surveillance in strengthening regional situational awareness and informing public health responses, while recognizing limitations related to representativeness and the absence of population denominators.

papers.title: Molecular Cloning and Reverse Genetics.
papers.abstract: This chapter describes a detailed molecular biology protocol for introducing specific point mutations into the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genome using a reverse genetics strategy. The method utilizes an overlapping PCR-based approach to generate a mutated DNA fragment, which is then cloned into a pre-engineered CHIKV infectious clone plasmid. The protocol covers all major steps, from the initial PCRs to create the mutated insert to its digestion and ligation into the vector. It also includes procedures for bacterial transformation, colony screening via PCR and Sanger sequencing to confirm the mutation, and plasmid purification via miniprep. The document is structured with a clear introduction, a list of all required reagents and equipment, and a step-by-step methods section.

papers.title: Screening of Antiviral Agents Against CHIKV Using Reporter Virus.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) causes a disease characterized by chronic musculoskeletal inflammation for which specific antivirals are not yet available. Currently, a supportive therapy to alleviate fever and pain is used, but it does not limit viral replication or the persistence of chronic arthritis symptoms. Thus, the identification and development of new active molecules against CHIKV is urgently needed. Here, we present a cell-based methodology that enables the implementation of a rapid and cost-effective strategy for high- and medium-throughput screening (HTS) of compounds, including repurposed drugs or novel molecules. This methodology allows for the identification of novel antiviral hits with a good activity and selectivity profile against CHIKV.

papers.title: Epitope Tagging and Coimmunoprecipitation to Identify Viral Protein Interactors.
papers.abstract: Affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) is a powerful proteomic approach for dissecting the interaction network between virus and host. Traditional AP-MS employs overexpression of viral proteins as baits to enrich host interactors. However, overexpressed viral proteins may mislocalize to inappropriate cellular compartments and trigger endoplasmic reticulum stress by overwhelming the protein-folding machinery, which leads to false identification of host factors. To overcome these limitations, we introduce an AP-MS strategy based on direct infection with an epitope-tagged chikungunya virus (CHIKV/myc-E2), which we used to successfully uncover two new antiviral factors in CHIKV cellular reservoirs-macrophages. In this protocol, we will describe this technique step by step: (1) design and construction of myc-tagged virus by advanced multi-fragment assembly, (2) in vitro transcription and preparation of infectious myc-tagged virus stocks, and (3) immunoprecipitation of myc-tagged viral protein and its interactome for mass spectrometry analysis. This strategy enables accurate identification of viral interactors in a physiologically relevant context, providing a framework for future proteomic studies using tagged viruses.

papers.title: A Restriction-Free Cloning Approach for Molecular Engineering of Plasmids.
papers.abstract: Molecular cloning by PCR amplification using a highly processive, high-fidelity DNA polymerase represents a robust and versatile technique for the precise manipulation of nucleic acid sequences. This approach enables the insertion, replacement, or modification of specific DNA fragments within a cloning vector, thereby generating an accurate copy of a gene or viral segment for downstream applications, such as protein expression, site-directed mutagenesis, and structural or functional analyses. The use of processive, high-fidelity polymerases significantly reduces the occurrence of base substitution errors, ensuring sequence integrity throughout the amplification process. Traditionally, restriction enzymes have been employed to facilitate directional cloning; however, alternative methods allow for mutagenesis without the need for unique and specific restriction sites and can be applied to virtually any cloning or seamless DNA assembly strategy. In this chapter, we describe a restriction enzyme-free and ligation-free PCR-based protocol widely applicable to any circular vector. This method enables targeted mutagenesis of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genome, offering a fast, efficient, and reliable strategy for generating mutant constructs suitable for virological and molecular studies.

papers.title_zh: 质粒分子工程的无限制克隆方法。
papers.source_body_en: Molecular cloning by PCR amplification using a highly processive, high-fidelity DNA polymerase represents a robust and versatile technique for the precise manipulation of nucleic acid sequences. This approach enables the insertion, replacement, or modification of specific DNA fragments within a cloning vector, thereby generating an accurate copy of a gene or viral segment for downstream applications, such as protein expression, site-directed mutagenesis, and structural or functional analyses. The use of processive, high-fidelity polymerases significantly reduces the occurrence of base substitution errors, ensuring sequence integrity throughout the amplification process. Traditionally, restriction enzymes have been employed to facilitate directional cloning; however, alternative methods allow for mutagenesis without the need for unique and specific restriction sites and can be applied to virtually any cloning or seamless DNA assembly strategy. In this chapter, we describe a restriction enzyme-free and ligation-free PCR-based protocol widely applicable to any circular vector. This method enables targeted mutagenesis of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genome, offering a fast, efficient, and reliable strategy for generating mutant constructs suitable for virological and molecular studies.
papers.abstract_zh: 使用高持续性、高保真度 DNA 聚合酶通过 PCR 扩增进行分子克隆代表了一种用于精确操作核酸序列的稳健且通用的技术。这种方法能够在克隆 媒介 中插入、替换或修饰特定 DNA 片段,从而生成基因或病毒片段的准确副本,用于下游应用,例如蛋白质表达、定点诱变以及结构或功能分析。使用持续的高保真聚合酶可显着减少碱基替换错误的发生,确保整个扩增过程中的序列完整性。传统上,限制性内切酶被用来促进定向克隆。然而,替代方法允许诱变,而不需要独特和特定的限制位点,并且可以应用于几乎任何克隆或无缝 DNA 组装策略。在本章中,我们描述了一种基于无限制性内切酶和无连接 PCR 的方案,广泛适用于任何环状 媒介。该方法能够对 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 基因组 进行定向诱变,为生成适合病毒学和分子研究的突变体构建体提供快速、高效和可靠的策略。

papers.title: Updated checklist of Culicidae (Diptera) in Adana Province, Türkiye, with the first record of Aedes albopictus
papers.abstract: Aedes (Ae.) albopictus is an invasive mosquito species of major public health concern due to its ability to transmit arboviruses such as dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. Although its expansion in Europe and Türkiye is well documented, data from the eastern Mediterranean region remain limited. This study aimed to update the Culicidae fauna of Adana Province and determine the occurrence and establishment status of Ae. albopictus . Field surveys were conducted at 30 sites across urban, peri-urban, agricultural, and coastal habitats in Adana Province, Türkiye, during the summer of 2024. Adult mosquitoes were collected using CDC miniature light traps, while immature stages were sampled from aquatic habitats and reared to adulthood under laboratory conditions. Species identification was performed using standard morphological keys and taxonomic references. A total of 2,130 specimens representing seven mosquito species and four genera were identified. Culex (Cx.) pipiens was the dominant species, whereas Ae. albopictus accounted for 227 individuals (10.64%). The species was detected in all surveyed districts (Seyhan, Yüreğir, Karataş, and Yumurtalık). Both field-collected adults and laboratory-emerged specimens confirmed the presence of all developmental stages, with higher abundance in Seyhan District indicating localized population foci. The detection of multiple life stages provides strong evidence for the establishment of Ae. albopictus in Adana Province, representing a significant southward expansion in Türkiye. These findings fill a critical gap in national distribution data and highlight ongoing invasion dynamics in the eastern Mediterranean region. Enhanced surveillance and integrated vector management are required due to its epidemiological importance.

Page 1/12 Abstract Aedes (Ae.) albopictus is an invasive mosquito species of major public health concern due to its ability to transmit arboviruses such as dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. Although its expansion in Europe and Türkiye is well documented, data from the eastern Mediterranean region remain limited. This study aimed to update the Culicidae fauna of Adana Province and determine the occurrence and establishment status of Ae. albopictus. Field surveys were conducted at 30 sites across urban, peri-urban, agricultural, and coastal habitats in Adana Province, Türkiye, during the summer of 2024. Adult mosquitoes were collected using CDC miniature light traps, while immature stages were sampled from aquatic habitats and reared to adulthood under laboratory conditions. Species identification was performed using standard morphological keys and taxonomic references. A total of 2,130 specimens representing seven mosquito species and four genera were identified. Culex (Cx.) pipiens was the dominant species, whereas Ae. albopictus accounted for 227 individuals (10.64%). The species was detected in all surveyed districts (Seyhan, Yüreğir, Karataş, and Yumurtalık). Both field-collected adults and laboratory-emerged specimens confirmed the presence of all developmental stages, with higher abundance in Seyhan District indicating localized population foci. The detection of multiple life stages provides strong evidence for the establishment of Ae. albopictus in Adana Province, representing a significant southward expansion in Türkiye. These findings fill a critical gap in national distribution data and highlight ongoing invasion dynamics in the eastern Mediterranean region. Enhanced surveillance and integrated vector management are required due to its epidemiological importance. Introduction Vector-borne diseases represent a major global public health challenge, accounting for more than 17% of all infectious diseases and causing over 700,000 deaths annually worldwide. Among arthropod vectors, mosquitoes are considered the most important group from a public health perspective because they transmit a wide range of pathogens responsible for diseases such as malaria, dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever, West Nile fever, and Zika virus disease (World Health Organization, 2024). Species of the genus Aedes (Ae.) (Diptera: Culicidae) are among the most important mosquito vectors of human arboviruses. In particular, Ae. aegypti and Ae. albopictus are responsible for the transmission of several medically important viruses, including dengue virus (DENV), chikungunya virus (CHIKV), zika virus (ZIKV), and yellow fever virus (YFV). Their close association with human settlements, adaptation to artificial breeding sites, and high ecological plasticity have contributed substantially to their epidemiological importance and global expansion (Bonizzoni et al. 2013; Kraemer et al. 2015). As a consequence of this global expansion, invasive Aedes mosquito populations have shown a marked increase across the European continent in recent decades. To date, at least six non-native mosquito species have been reported as introduced or established in Europe, including Ae. atropalpus, Ae. japonicus, Ae. koreicus, Ae. aegypti, Ae. albopictus, and Ae. triseriatus (Vasquez et al. 2023). Among invasive mosquito species, Ae. albopictus is considered one of the most rapidly expanding globally, owing to its high ecological plasticity, desiccation-resistant eggs, and ability to survive under temperate climatic conditions (Kraemer et al. 2019). In Europe, this species has been associated with autochthonous outbreaks of dengue in countries including France, Italy, Croatia, and Spain, as well as chikungunya outbreaks in France and Italy, highlighting its established role in local transmission cycles (Kraemer et al. 2019; ECDC, 2026). Consequently, Ae. albopictus is now widely established across large parts of Europe, particularly in Mediterranean and temperate regions, with ongoing geographic expansion. Page 2/12 Furthermore, the public health significance of Aedes mosquitoes is also recognized in neighboring regions such as Türkiye, where Culicidae species have been extensively documented in terms of distribution and vectorial capacity (Şimşek & Günay, 2017). The potential for Zika virus (ZIKV) transmission remains a concern in areas receiving imported cases, as experimental studies have demonstrated that both Ae. aegypti and Ae. albopictus are capable of supporting ZIKV infection and transmission under suitable environmental conditions (Ciota et al. 2017; Gómez et al. 2022). Following its first detection in Türkiye in Edirne in 2011 (Öter et al. 2013), Ae. albopictus has progressively expanded its distribution across the country, with established records reported from the Marmara, Black Sea, and Aegean regions (Demirci et al. 2021; ECDC, 2026). Despite this documented spread, evidence regarding the presence and local establishment of Ae. albopictus in the eastern Mediterranean region of Türkiye, particularly in Adana Province, remained limited prior to recent observations (Şimşek & Yavaşoğlu, 2023). The aim of this study was to investigate the occurrence and field-based distribution of Ae. albopictus in Adana Province, southern Türkiye, and to provide baseline entomological data for future surveillance and risk assessment of this invasive vector species. Methodology Study Area The study was conducted across 30 geographically predefined sites located in the districts of Seyhan, Yüreğir, Sarıçam, Karataş, and Yumurtalık in Adana Province, Türkiye. Sampling sites were distributed across a broad spatial gradient and were georeferenced using GPS coordinates. The study area is situated in the eastern Mediterranean region and is characterized by a Mediterranean climate with hot, dry summers and mild, rainy winters (Köppen–Geiger classification: Csa). The elevation of the sampling sites ranged from 1 to 88 m above sea level. (Fig. 1). Mosquito Sampling, Rearing and Morphological Identification Mosquito sampling was conducted across diverse ecological settings, including residential areas, agricultural landscapes, and peri-urban environments, all of which are considered suitable habitats for the establishment and persistence of invasive mosquito species such as Ae. albopictus. Field surveys were performed during the summer of 2024 (June–August), and each of the 30 predefined sampling sites was visited three times. At each sampling occasion, collections were conducted over five consecutive days and five nights, ensuring standardized temporal coverage across sites. Adult mosquito sampling was carried out using CDC miniature light traps (Model 512, John W. Hock Company, Gainesville, FL, USA) (Fig. 2A and 2B), which were deployed at each site. Four traps were used per site per sampling event, resulting in a total of 360 trap-night samples across the study area. Traps were positioned at approximately 1.5 m above ground level and operated for 24 h. Specimens collected were preserved in 70% ethanol and transported to the laboratory for further processing. In addition to adult collections, immature stages were surveyed in a variety of natural and artificial aquatic habitats, including irrigation canals, temporary rain pools, stagnant water accumulations, and domestic water storage containers (Fig. 2C-2F). Larvae and pupae were collected using standard larval dippers (Fig. 2G) and transported to the laboratory in labeled containers. Following transport, specimens were maintained in water-filled containers in a sheltered outdoor area within the Faculty of Medicine campus and allowed to complete their development under ambient environmental Page 3/12 conditions. Individuals were monitored regularly until adult emergence, and the emerged adults were subsequently collected for species identification (WHO, 2005; Silver, 2008) (Fig. 2H and 2I). Species identification of both field-collected adults and adults emerging from field-collected immature stages was performed under a stereomicroscope using standard morphological identification keys, including Merdivenci (1984), Şimşek and Günay (2017), and the MosKeyTool interactive identification platform. Results A total of 2,130 mosquito specimens were collected during the study period through direct adult sampling and immature-stage collections followed by laboratory rearing to adulthood. Seven mosquito species belonging to four genera were identified. Species composition analysis showed that Culex (Cx.) pipiens was the predominant species, accounting for 964 specimens (45.23%) of the total collection. The second most abundant species was Cx. territans, represented by 450 specimens (21.13%). Ae. albopictus ranked third in abundance with 227 specimens (10.64%), followed by Ae. caspius with 200 specimens (9.39%). Anopheles maculipennis and Cx. quinquefasciatus accounted for 170 (7.98%) and 110 (5.16%) specimens, respectively, whereas Culiseta morsitans was the least frequently encountered species, represented by only 10 specimens (0.47%). A total of 227 Aedes (Ae.) albopictus specimens were recorded from 30 sampling locations distributed across the Seyhan, Yüreğir, Karataş, and Yumurtalık districts of Adana Province. Of these, 82 specimens were collected as adults in the field using CDC light traps, whereas 145 specimens were obtained through laboratory rearing of immature stages collected from breeding habitats. The species was detected across all four surveyed districts and was recorded from a variety of habitat types, including urban residential areas, peri-urban settlements, agricultural zones, and coastal localities. The highest abundances were observed in Seyhan District, particularly in Çamlıtepe, where 14 field-collected adults and 18 reared adults were obtained, and in Balcalı, where 11 field-collected adults and 14 reared adults were recorded. Additional positive sampling sites were distributed across Yüreğir, Karataş, and Yumurtalık districts. The spatial distribution of Ae. albopictus across sampling locations is presented in Table 1. Adult and laboratory-emerged adult specimens of Ae. albopictus were confirmed based on direct morphological examination under a stereomicroscope. Diagnostic characters observed included a black integument with a distinct longitudinal median stripe of silvery-white scales on the scutum, dark legs with white tarsal banding, and abdominal tergites with pale scale patches consistent with species-level diagnostic morphology. These characters were consistently observed in both field-collected adults and laboratory-emerged specimens, supporting species-level identification of Ae. albopictus from multiple sampling sites. The morphological characteristics of adult specimens are illustrated in Fig. 3. Discussion The present study provides the first confirmed record of Aedes (Ae.) albopictus in Adana Province, representing a significant southward extension of the known distribution of this invasive mosquito species in Türkiye. Since its initial detection in northwestern Türkiye in 2011 (Oter et al. 2013), Ae. albopictus has exhibited a progressive range expansion across the country, with established populations reported from the Black Sea and Aegean regions (Akiner et al. 2016; Şimşek and Günay, 2017; Demirci et al. 2021). However, prior to the present study, records from the eastern Mediterranean region remained absent, indicating a notable geographical gap in its documented distribution. The detection of Ae. albopictus in Adana therefore fills an important spatial discontinuity and confirms further expansion toward southern Türkiye. Page 4/12 The establishment of Ae. albopictus in Adana is consistent with its well-documented ecological plasticity and adaptation to anthropogenic environments. The species is known to exploit artificial water containers, irrigation systems, and urban drainage structures, which facilitate population persistence in Mediterranean-type cities (Benedict et al. 2007; Bonizzoni et al. 2013; Ravasi et al. 2022). Additionally, the production of desiccation-resistant eggs enhances survival under seasonal climatic variability, promoting long-term establishment in temperate and semi-arid environments. Climatic suitability assessments further indicate that southern Türkiye provides favorable conditions for colonization due to extended warm seasons and increasing temperatures (Caminade et al. 2012; Merkenschlager et al. 2025). The simultaneous detection of field-collected adults and individuals emerging from laboratory-reared immature stages provides strong evidence of local reproduction and establishment of Ae. albopictus populations. In vector ecology, the presence of immature stages in breeding habitats is widely recognized as an indicator of autochthonous populations and sustained local reproduction (Pedric et al. 2014). Page 1/12 Abstract Aedes (Ae.) albopictus is an invasive mosquito species of major public health concern due to its ability to transmit arboviruses such as dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. Although its expansion in Europe and Türkiye is well documented, data from the eastern Mediterranean region remain limited. This study aimed to update the Culicidae fauna of Adana Province and determine the occurrence and establishment status of Ae. albopictus. Field surveys were conducted at 30 sites across urban, peri-urban, agricultural, and coastal habitats in Adana Province, Türkiye, during the summer of 2024. Adult mosquitoes were collected using CDC miniature light traps, while immature stages were sampled from aquatic habitats and reared to adulthood under laboratory conditions. Species identification was performed using standard morphological keys and taxonomic references. A total of 2,130 specimens representing seven mosquito species and four genera were identified. Culex (Cx.) pipiens was the dominant species, whereas Ae. albopictus accounted for 227 individuals (10.64%). The species was detected in all surveyed districts (Seyhan, Yüreğir, Karataş, and Yumurtalık). Both field-collected adults and laboratory-emerged specimens confirmed the presence of all developmental stages, with higher abundance in Seyhan District indicating localized population foci. The detection of multiple life stages provides strong evidence for the establishment of Ae. albopictus in Adana Province, representing a significant southward expansion in Türkiye. These findings fill a critical gap in national distribution data and highlight ongoing invasion dynamics in the eastern Mediterranean region. Enhanced surveillance and integrated vector management are required due to its epidemiological importance. Introduction Vector-borne diseases represent a major global public health challenge, accounting for more than 17% of all infectious diseases and causing over 700,000 deaths annually worldwide. Among arthropod vectors, mosquitoes are considered the most important group from a public health perspective because they transmit a wide range of pathogens responsible for diseases such as malaria, dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever, West Nile fever, and Zika virus disease (World Health Organization, 2024). Species of the genus Aedes (Ae.) (Diptera: Culicidae) are among the most important mosquito vectors of human arboviruses. In particular, Ae. aegypti and Ae. albopictus are responsible for the transmission of several medically important viruses, including dengue virus (DENV), chikungunya virus (CHIKV), zika virus (ZIKV), and yellow fever virus (YFV). Their close association with human settlements, adaptation to artificial breeding sites, and high ecological plasticity have contributed substantially to their epidemiological importance and global expansion (Bonizzoni et al. 2013; Kraemer et al. 2015). As a consequence of this global expansion, invasive Aedes mosquito populations have shown a marked increase across the European continent in recent decades. To date, at least six non-native mosquito species have been reported as introduced or established in Europe, including Ae. atropalpus, Ae. japonicus, Ae. koreicus, Ae. aegypti, Ae. albopictus, and Ae. triseriatus (Vasquez et al. 2023). Among invasive mosquito species, Ae. albopictus is considered one of the most rapidly expanding globally, owing to its high ecological plasticity, desiccation-resistant eggs, and ability to survive under temperate climatic conditions (Kraemer et al. 2019). In Europe, this species has been associated with autochthonous outbreaks of dengue in countries including France, Italy, Croatia, and Spain, as well as chikungunya outbreaks in France and Italy, highlighting its established role in local transmission cycles (Kraemer et al. 2019; ECDC, 2026). Consequently, Ae. albopictus is now widely established across large parts of Europe, particularly in Mediterranean and temperate regions, with ongoing geographic expansion. Page 2/12 Furthermore, the public health significance of Aedes mosquitoes is also recognized in neighboring regions such as Türkiye, where Culicidae species have been extensively documented in terms of distribution and vectorial capacity (Şimşek & Günay, 2017). The potential for Zika virus (ZIKV) transmission remains a concern in areas receiving imported cases, as experimental studies have demonstrated that both Ae. aegypti and Ae. albopictus are capable of supporting ZIKV infection and transmission under suitable environmental conditions (Ciota et al. 2017; Gómez et al. 2022). Following its first detection in Türkiye in Edirne in 2011 (Öter et al. 2013), Ae. albopictus has progressively expanded its distribution across the country, with established records reported from the Marmara, Black Sea, and Aegean regions (Demirci et al. 2021; ECDC, 2026). Despite this documented spread, evidence regarding the presence and local establishment of Ae. albopictus in the eastern Mediterranean region of Türkiye, particularly in Adana Province, remained limited prior to recent observations (Şimşek & Yavaşoğlu, 2023). The aim of this study was to investigate the occurrence and field-based distribution of Ae. albopictus in Adana Province, southern Türkiye, and to provide baseline entomological data for future surveillance and risk assessment of this invasive vector species. Methodology Study Area The study was conducted across 30 geographically predefined sites located in the districts of Seyhan, Yüreğir, Sarıçam, Karataş, and Yumurtalık in Adana Province, Türkiye. Sampling sites were distributed across a broad spatial gradient and were georeferenced using GPS coordinates. The study area is situated in the eastern Mediterranean region and is characterized by a Mediterranean climate with hot, dry summers and mild, rainy winters (Köppen–Geiger classification: Csa). The elevation of the sampling sites ranged from 1 to 88 m above sea level. (Fig. 1). Mosquito Sampling, Rearing and Morphological Identification Mosquito sampling was conducted across diverse ecological settings, including residential areas, agricultural landscapes, and peri-urban environments, all of which are considered suitable habitats for the establishment and persistence of invasive mosquito species such as Ae. albopictus. Field surveys were performed during the summer of 2024 (June–August), and each of the 30 predefined sampling sites was visited three times. At each sampling occasion, collections were conducted over five consecutive days and five nights, ensuring standardized temporal coverage across sites. Adult mosquito sampling was carried out using CDC miniature light traps (Model 512, John W. Hock Company, Gainesville, FL, USA) (Fig. 2A and 2B), which were deployed at each site. Four traps were used per site per sampling event, resulting in a total of 360 trap-night samples across the study area. Traps were positioned at approximately 1.5 m above ground level and operated for 24 h. Specimens collected were preserved in 70% ethanol and transported to the laboratory for further processing. In addition to adult collections, immature stages were surveyed in a variety of natural and artificial aquatic habitats, including irrigation canals, temporary rain pools, stagnant water accumulations, and domestic water storage containers (Fig. 2C-2F). analysis.summary_en: This study updates the Culicidae fauna of Adana Province, Türkiye, and confirms the establishment of Ae. albopictus, an invasive mosquito species capable of transmitting arboviruses like chikungunya. Field surveys across 30 sites in various habitats during the summer of 2024 identified 2,130 specimens, with Ae. albopictus accounting for 10.64% of the total. The species was detected in all surveyed districts, indicating localized population foci. The presence of multiple life stages supports its establishment in the region, marking a significant southward expansion in Türkiye. These findings emphasize the need for enhanced surveillance and vector management due to the public health risks associated with Ae. albopictus. However, the study's reliance on morphological identification limits the confidence in its conclusions, as molecular confirmation of CHIKV transmission was not provided.

papers.title: Provenance and competence for CHIKV and DENV of Aedes albopictus populations
papers.abstract: Aedes albopictus is one of the world’s most hazardous invasive species, increasingly implicated in the autochthonous transmission of Chikungunya (CHIKV) and Dengue (DENV) viruses in newly colonized areas. Since invading the Mediterranean Basin several in the early 1980s, recurrent introductions of distinct lineages have driven extensive genomic admixture within adventive populations. This study investigates whether and how the complex dynamics of these diverse genetic backgrounds have shaped variations in vector competence for CHIKV, DENV, and Zika (ZIKV) viruses. Using highly polymorphic simple sequence repeat (SSR) markers, we genotyped Ae. Albopictus samples from an ancestral population (Guangzhou, China) and ten adventive populations across five Mediterranean regions (Southern Switzerland, Northern/Central Italy, the Balkans, and Greece). Genetic ancestry and demographic histories were inferred using Bayesian STRUCTURE (v2.3.2.0) and DIYABC-RF. The association between population ancestry and vector competence for CHIKV (06.21), DENV-1, and ZIKV (PE243) was assessed using infection rate, dissemination efficiency, and transmission efficiency indices, analyzed via univariate and multivariate models. Combining historical records with demographic models revealed that the establishment of Ae. Albopictus in the Mediterranean was driven by chaotic, discontinuous lineage introductions and admixture events, resulting in high spatial and ancestry heterogeneity. Notably, this genetic heterogeneity significantly influences vector competence, in particular for CHIKV and DENV. Interestingly, populations in neighboring geographical areas with distinct ancestries exhibited drastically different competence profiles, whereas geographically distant populations sharing genetic ancestry displayed similar vector competence for CHIKV and DENV. Our findings demonstrate that the complex population dynamics and colonization history of Ae. Albopictus contributes to variation in vector competence, altering the geographical landscape of arboviral risk. These results underscore the urgent need for localized, geographically tailored vector control strategies in Europe, a region facing a rising trend of both imported and autochthonous arboviral infections.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究调查了不同遗传背景的复杂动态是否以及如何影响 媒介 对 CHIKV、DENV 和 ZIKV 病毒的能力的变化。白纹伊蚊是世界上最危险的入侵物种之一,在新殖民地区越来越多地与基孔肯雅热 (CHIKV) 和登革热 (DENV) 病毒的本土 传播 相关。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了来自祖先种群(中国广州)和五个地中海地区十个入侵种群的 Aedes albopictus 样本(南方瑞士、北/中意大利、巴尔干半岛和希腊)。自1980年代初入侵地中海盆地以来,不同谱系的反复引入导致了入侵种群中的广泛基因组混合。
elements_zh.methods: 使用感染率、传播效率和 传播 效率指数评估人群血统与 媒介 对 CHIKV (06.21)、DENV-1 和 ZIKV (PE243) 能力之间的关联,并通过单变量和多变量模型进行分析。使用贝叶斯结构 (v2.3.2.0) 和 DIYABC-RF 推断遗传祖先和人口统计历史。
elements_zh.main_results: 将历史记录与人口模型相结合表明,Ae 的建立。地中海的白纹伊蚊是由混乱、不连续的谱系引入和混合事件驱动的,导致了高度的空间和祖先异质性。值得注意的是,这种遗传异质性显着影响 媒介 的能力,特别是对于 CHIKV 和 DENV。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 具有不同血统的邻近地理区域的人群表现出截然不同的能力特征,而具有遗传血统的地理遥远的人群则表现出类似的 媒介 对 CHIKV 和 DENV 的能力。我们的研究结果表明,伊蚊复杂的种群动态和定殖历史。白纹伊蚊导致 媒介 能力的变化,改变虫媒病毒风险的地理格局。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果强调了欧洲迫切需要本地化、按地理位置定制的 媒介 控制策略,该地区面临着输入性和本土虫媒病毒感染的上升趋势。
